abomasnow.description: A powerful Pokémon that can split huge boulders with ease. Dislikes associating with others and chooses to live quietly deep within the mountains, playing with the snow.

abra.description: Spends 18 hours of the day sleeping. Even while asleep, Abra can control its psychic powers—should danger approach, the Pokémon will simply teleport away.

absol.description: Because of this Pokémon’s ability to detect danger, people mistook Absol as a bringer of doom.

accelgor.description: Discarding its shell made it nimble. To keep itself from dehydrating, it wraps its body in bands of membrane.

aegislash-shield.description: Its potent spectral powers allow it to manipulate others. It once used its powers to force people and Pokémon to build a kingdom to its liking.

aerodactyl.description: Aerodactyl’s sawlike fangs can shred skin to tatters—even the skin of Steel-type Pokémon.

aggron.description: Long ago, there was a king who wore a helmet meant to resemble the head of an Aggron. He was trying to channel the Pokémon’s strength.

aipom.description: This treetop dweller possesses a tail as dexterous as a hand. Ancient writings describe this Pokémon as a one-armed oddity.

alakazam.description: The longer Alakazam lives, the larger and heavier its head becomes. Our tests have shown that the strength of its psychic powers correlates positively to the weight of its head.

alcremie.description: When Alcremie is content, the cream it secretes from its hands becomes sweeter and richer.

alomomola.description: The reason it helps Pokémon in a weakened condition is that any Pokémon coming after them may also attack Alomomola.

altaria.description: This Pokémon has a kind disposition, but if it’s provoked, it will threaten opponents with shrill cries before attacking them without mercy.

amaura.description: Amaura is an ancient Pokémon that has gone extinct. Specimens of this species can sometimes be found frozen in ice.

ambipom.description: To affirm their kinship, members of this species will form a ring by linking their newly doubled tails together. On rare occasions, humans have been accepted into such rings.

amoonguss.description: Amoonguss generally doesn’t move much. It tends to stand still near Poké Balls that have been dropped on the ground.

ampharos.description: Its tail shines bright and strong. It has been prized since long ago as a beacon for sailors.

annihilape.description: It imbues its fists with the power of the rage that it kept hidden in its heart. Opponents struck by these imbued fists will be shattered to their core.

anorith.description: Anorith can swim swiftly by pulling its eight wings through the water like oars on a boat. This Pokémon is an ancestor of modern bug Pokémon.

appletun.description: Its body is covered in sweet nectar, and the skin on its back is especially yummy. Children used to have it as a snack.

applin.description: As soon as it’s born, it burrows into an apple. Not only does the apple serve as its food source, but the flavor of the fruit determines its evolution.

araquanid.description: It acts as a caretaker for Dewpider, putting them inside its bubble and letting them eat any leftover food.

arbok.description: The frightening patterns on its belly have been studied. Six variations have been confirmed.

arboliva.description: This Pokémon drives back enemies by launching its rich, aromatic oil at them with enough force to smash a boulder.

arcanine.description: Snaps at its foes with fangs cloaked in blazing flame. Despite its bulk, it deftly feints every which way, leading opponents on a deceptively merry chase as it all but dances around them.

arceus.description: It is the heavenly fount from which pours the light that shines across Hisui. Its luminance guides and protects all Pokémon. Hisuian mythology states that Arceus is the creator of all things.

archaludon.description: It digs holes on mountains, searching for food. It’s so durable that being caught in a cave-in won’t faze it.

archen.description: Archen is said to be the ancestor of bird Pokémon. It lived in treetops, eating berries and bug Pokémon.

archeops.description: Though capable of flight, Archeops was apparently better at hunting on the ground.

arctibax.description: It attacks with the blade of its frozen dorsal fin by doing a front flip in the air. Arctibax’s strong back and legs allow it to pull off this technique.

arctovish.description: The skin on its face is impervious to attack, but breathing difficulties made this Pokémon go extinct anyway.

arctozolt.description: This Pokémon lived on prehistoric seashores and was able to preserve food with the ice on its body. It went extinct because it moved so slowly.

ariados.description: It spews threads from its mouth to catch its prey. When night falls, it leaves its web to go hunt aggressively.

armaldo.description: Though it lives on land, it’s also a good swimmer. It dives into the ocean in search of prey, using its sharp claws to take down its quarry.

armarouge.description: This Pokémon clads itself in armor that has been fortified by psychic and fire energy, and it shoots blazing fireballs.

aromatisse.description: The scents Aromatisse can produce range from sweet smells that bolster allies to foul smells that sap an opponent’s will to fight.

aron.description: When Aron evolves, its steel armor peels off. In ancient times, people would collect Aron’s shed armor and make good use of it in their daily lives.

arrokuda.description: After it’s eaten its fill, its movements become extremely sluggish. That’s when Cramorant swallows it up.

articuno.description: This Pokémon can control ice at will. Articuno is said to live in snowy mountains riddled with permafrost.

audino.description: This Pokémon has a kind heart. By touching with its feelers, Audino can gauge other creatures’ feelings and physical conditions.

aurorus.description: When gripped by rage, Aurorus will emanate freezing air, covering everything around it in ice.

avalugg.description: The armor of ice covering its lower jaw puts steel to shame and can shatter rocks with ease. This Pokémon barrels along steep mountain paths, cleaving through the deep snow.

axew.description: They play with each other by knocking their large tusks together. Their tusks break sometimes, but they grow back so quickly that it isn’t a concern.

azelf.description: The dreaded Being of Willpower. Legends tell of this Pokémon manipulating the will of its adversaries and turning them into puppets of its own.

azumarill.description: These Pokémon create air-filled bubbles. When Azurill play in rivers, Azumarill will cover them with these bubbles.

azurill.description: Although Azurill are normally docile, an angry one will swing around the big ball on its tail and try to smash its opponents.

bagon.description: Bagon is a solitary Pokémon that doesn’t form groups with others of its kind. It also has a head hard enough to cleave a boulder in one strike.

baltoy.description: It was discovered in ancient ruins. While moving, it constantly spins. It stands on one foot even when asleep.

banette.description: Resentment at being cast off made it spring into being. Some say that treating it well will satisfy it, and it will once more become a stuffed toy.

barbaracle.description: Having an eye on each palm allows it to keep watch in all directions. In a pinch, its limbs start to act on their own to ensure the enemy’s defeat.

barboach.description: Makes its home in swamps with murky water. The poor visibility hides this Pokémon from predators, and the slime on its body makes grasping it difficult.

barraskewda.description: It spins its tail fins to propel itself, surging forward at speeds of over 100 knots before ramming prey and spearing into them.

basculegion-male.description: Clads itself in the souls of comrades that perished before fulfilling their goals of journeying upstream. No other species throughout all Hisui's rivers is Basculegion's equal.

basculin-red-striped.description: Though it differs from other Basculin in several respects, including demeanor—this one is gentle—I have categorized it as a regional form given the vast array of shared qualities.

bastiodon.description: Its face is sturdy—as strong as diamond—and this hardness offers a very stable defense. Much about this species is still unknown, such as its natural habitat.

baxcalibur.description: It launches itself into battle by flipping upside down and spewing frigid air from its mouth. It finishes opponents off with its dorsal blade.

bayleef.description: Bayleef’s neck is ringed by curled-up leaves. Inside each tubular leaf is a small shoot of a tree. The fragrance of this shoot makes people peppy.

beartic.description: It swims energetically through frigid seas. When it gets tired, it freezes the seawater with its breath so it can rest on the ice.

beautifly.description: A colorful and incredibly beautiful but also greedy Pokémon. In an effort to keep its favorite food all to itself, it will chase away Combee as they try to gather nectar.

beedrill.description: It has three poisonous stingers on its forelegs and its tail. They are used to jab its enemy repeatedly.

beheeyem.description: Sometimes found drifting above wheat fields, this Pokémon can control the memories of its opponents.

beldum.description: The cells in this Pokémon’s body are composed of magnetic material. Instead of blood, magnetic forces flow through Beldum’s body.

bellibolt.description: What appear to be eyeballs are actually organs for discharging the electricity generated by Bellibolt’s belly-button dynamo.

bellossom.description: Bellossom gather at times and appear to dance. They say that the dance is a ritual to summon the sun.

bellsprout.description: Prefers hot and humid places. It ensnares tiny bugs with its vines and devours them.

bergmite.description: Lives on mountains blanketed in perennial snow. It freezes water vapor in the air to make the ice helmet that it dons for defense.

bewear.description: The moves it uses to take down its prey would make a martial artist jealous. It tucks subdued prey under its arms to carry them to its nest.

bibarel.description: Bibarel fur repels water and is also a fantastic material for heat retention. These Pokémon create dams on rivers to live in.

bidoof.description: Bidoof has an unsophisticated face and is rarely flustered by anything. There have been incidents involving Bidoof sauntering into villages and gnawing on the houses without a single care.

binacle.description: If the two don’t work well together, both their offense and defense fall apart. Without good teamwork, they won’t survive.

bisharp.description: Violent conflicts erupt between Bisharp and Fraxure over places where sharpening stones can be found.

blacephalon.description: A UB that appeared from an Ultra Wormhole, it causes explosions, then takes advantage of opponents’ surprise to rob them of their vitality.

blastoise.description: The rocket cannons on its shell fire jets of water capable of punching holes through thick steel.

blaziken.description: Blaziken has incredibly strong legs—it can easily clear a 30-story building in one leap. This Pokémon’s blazing punches leave its foes scorched and blackened.

blipbug.description: Often found in gardens, this Pokémon has hairs on its body that it uses to assess its surroundings.

blissey.description: A kindhearted Pokémon that will care for any sick person or Pokémon until their health improves. The eggs it lays are delicious and bring good fortune to those who eat them.

blitzle.description: Its mane shines when it discharges electricity. They use the frequency and rhythm of these flashes to communicate.

boldore.description: It relies on sound in order to monitor what’s in its vicinity. When angered, it will attack without ever changing the direction it’s facing.

boltund.description: It sends electricity through its legs to boost their strength. Running at top speed, it easily breaks 50 mph.

bombirdier.description: Bombirdier uses the apron on its chest to bundle up food, which it carries back to its nest. It enjoys dropping things that make loud noises.

bonsly.description: Its tears elicit sympathy from those who see them, but do not be deceived! This expulsion of body water is merely a physiological mechanism for keeping itself in good health.

bouffalant.description: These Pokémon live in herds of about 20 individuals. Bouffalant that betray the herd will lose the hair on their heads for some reason.

bounsweet.description: When under attack, it secretes a sweet and delicious sweat. The scent only calls more enemies to it.

braixen.description: When the twig is plucked from its tail, friction sets the twig alight. The flame is used to send signals to its allies.

brambleghast.description: Brambleghast wanders around arid regions. On rare occasions, mass outbreaks of these Pokémon will bury an entire town.

bramblin.description: Not even Bramblin knows where it is headed as it tumbles across the wilderness, blown by the wind. It loathes getting wet.

braviary.description: Screaming a bloodcurdling battle cry, this huge and ferocious bird Pokémon goes out on the hunt. It blasts lakes with shock waves, then scoops up any prey that float to the water's surface.

breloom.description: The seeds ringing Breloom’s tail are made of hardened toxic spores. It is horrible to eat the seeds. Just taking a bite of this Pokémon’s seed will cause your stomach to rumble.

brionne.description: On nights when the sea is calm, Brionne dance with one another to the singing of the Primarina that’s leading them.

bronzong.description: Some believe that its bell-like cry opens holes to another world. It has been revered as a deity since ancient times.

bronzor.description: Floats using a mysterious energy. The pattern engraved upon its back is held as sacred and can sometimes be found in imagery from ancient cemeteries and other such timeworn places.

brute-bonnet.description: It bears a slight resemblance to a Pokémon described in a dubious magazine as a cross between a dinosaur and a mushroom.

bruxish.description: Its skin is thick enough to fend off Mareanie’s spikes. With its robust teeth, Bruxish crunches up the spikes and eats them.

budew.description: When the sun's light strengthens, the bud atop this Pokémon's head opens. This is a sign to the people that the harsh winter is over, and the season of budding has begun.

buizel.description: It moves freely in the water by spinning its forked tail for propulsion. The resemblance to the screw of a steamboat is coincidental.

bulbasaur.description: While it is young, it uses the nutrients that are stored in the seed on its back in order to grow.

buneary.description: My hypothesis as to why Buneary rolls up its ears is that its hearing is far too keen. I surmise that the Pokémon protects its hearing by limiting the sound that may enter its ears.

bunnelby.description: It’s very sensitive to danger. The sound of Corviknight’s flapping will have Bunnelby digging a hole to hide underground in moments.

burmy.description: If its cloak is even slightly damaged, Burmy will immediately repair it with whatever is close at hand. The Pokémon within the cloak is scrawny and vulnerable to the cold.

butterfree.description: It collects honey every day. It rubs honey onto the hairs on its legs to carry it back to its nest.

buzzwole.description: Buzzwole goes around showing off its abnormally swollen muscles. It is one kind of Ultra Beast.

cacnea.description: The more arid and harsh the environment, the more pretty and fragrant a flower Cacnea grows. This Pokémon battles by wildly swinging its thorny arms.

cacturne.description: If a traveler is going through a desert in the thick of night, Cacturne will follow in a ragtag group. The Pokémon are biding their time, waiting for the traveler to tire and become incapable of moving.

calyrex.description: Calyrex is known in legend as a king that ruled over Galar in ancient times. It has the power to cause hearts to mend and plants to spring forth.

camerupt.description: The humps on Camerupt’s back are formed by a transformation of its bones. They sometimes blast out molten magma. This Pokémon apparently erupts often when it is enraged.

capsakid.description: Traditional Paldean dishes can be extremely spicy because they include the shed front teeth of Capsakid among their ingredients.

carbink.description: It’s said that somewhere in the world, there’s a mineral vein housing a large pack of slumbering Carbink. It’s also said that this pack has a queen.

carkol.description: By rapidly rolling its legs, it can travel at over 18 mph. The temperature of the flames it breathes exceeds 1,800 degrees Fahrenheit.

carnivine.description: Though this is a plant Pokémon, it has a gluttonous and unruly temperament. Carnivine attacks its prey with its cavernous maw wide open.

carracosta.description: This Pokémon emerges from the water in search of prey despite the fact that it moves more slowly on land.

carvanha.description: These Pokémon have sharp fangs and powerful jaws. Sailors avoid Carvanha dens at all costs.

cascoon.description: The silk coating its body is thin but sufficiently strong. Cascoon's silk has a luster and texture superior to that of Silcoon's, and clothes made using Cascoon silk are regarded as top-notch.

castform.description: Its form changes depending on the weather. The rougher conditions get, the rougher Castform’s disposition!

caterpie.description: Its short feet are tipped with suction pads that enable it to tirelessly climb slopes and walls.

celebi.description: This Pokémon traveled through time to come from the future. It bolsters grass and trees with its own strength, and it can heal wounds, too.

celesteela.description: Although it’s alien to this world and a danger here, it’s apparently a common organism in the world where it normally lives.

centiskorch.description: While its burning body is already dangerous on its own, this excessively hostile Pokémon also has large and very sharp fangs.

ceruledge.description: An old set of armor steeped in grudges caused this Pokémon’s evolution. Ceruledge cuts its enemies to pieces without mercy.

cetitan.description: Ice energy builds up in the horn on its upper jaw, causing the horn to reach cryogenic temperatures that freeze its surroundings.

cetoddle.description: It lives in frigid regions in pods of five or so individuals. It loves the minerals found in snow and ice.

chandelure.description: In homes illuminated by Chandelure instead of lights, funerals were a constant occurrence— or so it’s said.

chansey.description: This purehearted Pokémon shares its eggs with the injured.

charcadet.description: Its firepower increases when it fights, reaching over 1,800 degrees Fahrenheit. It likes berries that are rich in fat.

charizard.description: Its wings can carry this Pokémon close to an altitude of 4,600 feet. It blows out fire at very high temperatures.

charjabug.description: Its digestive processes convert the leaves it eats into electricity. An electric sac in its belly stores the electricity for later use.

charmander.description: From the time it is born, a flame burns at the tip of its tail. Its life would end if the flame were to go out.

charmeleon.description: If it becomes agitated during battle, it spouts intense flames, incinerating its surroundings.

chatot.description: A versatile performer skilled in the imitation of human speech. It is said that older, more experienced Chatot can even understand the meaning of the words they mimic.

cherrim.description: Motionless, save for the occasional quiver. A rich array of Pokémon can be found gathered around it, drawn by the scent exuded from Cherrim's folded petals.

cherubi.description: Once the fruit growing alongside the main body is large and plump, Cherubi will use the nutrients within to evolve. The fruit then detaches, becoming nourishment for other creatures.

chesnaught.description: When it takes a defensive posture with its fists guarding its face, it could withstand a bomb blast.

chespin.description: Such a thick shell of wood covers its head and back that even a direct hit from a truck wouldn’t faze it.

chewtle.description: It starts off battles by attacking with its rock-hard horn, but as soon as the opponent flinches, this Pokémon bites down and never lets go.

chi-yu.description: The envy accumulated within curved beads that sparked multiple conflicts has clad itself in fire and become a Pokémon.

chien-pao.description: The hatred of those who perished by the sword long ago has clad itself in snow and become a Pokémon.

chikorita.description: In battle, Chikorita waves its leaf around to keep the foe at bay. However, a sweet fragrance also wafts from the leaf, becalming the battling Pokémon and creating a cozy, friendly atmosphere all around.

chimchar.description: Full of vigor and always in high spirits. It was once known by the name ”Lantern-Tail” and feared as some kind of apparition.

chimecho.description: Can emit waves of air powerful enough to knock out prey taller than itself. I hypothesize that it amplifies the faint sound of wind within its body.

chinchou.description: On the dark ocean floor, its only means of communication is its constantly flashing lights.

chingling.description: This Pokémon gave me an excruciating headache when it seemingly cried out without making a sound. Perhaps there are some sounds that the human ear is simply incapable of hearing.

cinccino.description: A special oil that seeps through their fur helps them avoid attacks. The oil fetches a high price at market.

cinderace.description: It’s skilled at both offense and defense, and it gets pumped up when cheered on. But if it starts showboating, it could put itself in a tough spot.

clamperl.description: Clamperl’s pearls are exceedingly precious. They can be more than 10 times as costly as Shellder’s pearls.

clauncher.description: By detonating gas that accumulates in its right claw, this Pokémon launches water like a bullet. This is how Clauncher defeats its enemies.

clawitzer.description: Clawitzer’s right arm is a cannon that launches projectiles made of seawater. Shots from a Clawitzer’s cannon arm can sink a tanker.

claydol.description: It appears to have been born from clay dolls made by ancient people. It uses telekinesis to float and move.

clefable.description: Legend says that on clear, quiet nights, it listens for the voices of its kin living on the moon. I, too, often think of my homeland, so far away.

clefairy.description: It can be found in quiet mountain areas on a full moon's night. Its dancing and its tiny, faintly glowing wings confer upon it a lovely fairylike quality.

cleffa.description: In silhouette, they resemble twinkling starlight. When shooting stars rain from the night sky, Cleffa gather in numbers and dance as though they are indeed incarnations of the stars.

clobbopus.description: Its tentacles tear off easily, but it isn’t alarmed when that happens—it knows they’ll grow back. It’s about as smart as a three-year-old.

clodsire.description: It lives at the bottom of ponds and swamps. It will carry Wooper on its back and ferry them across water from one shore to the other.

cloyster.description: Once it slams its shell shut, it is impossible to open, even by those with superior strength.

coalossal.description: While it’s engaged in battle, its mountain of coal will burn bright red, sending off sparks that scorch the surrounding area.

cobalion.description: From the moment it’s born, this Pokémon radiates the air of a leader. Its presence will calm even vicious foes.

cofagrigus.description: There are many depictions of Cofagrigus decorating ancient tombs. They’re symbols of the wealth that kings of bygone eras had.

combee.description: They swear fealty to a queen Pokémon and work diligently to gather nectar. Each swarm produces a different flavor of honey.

combusken.description: Combusken battles with the intensely hot flames it spews from its beak and with outstandingly destructive kicks. This Pokémon’s cry is very loud and distracting.

comfey.description: These Pokémon smell very nice. All Comfey wear different flowers, so each of these Pokémon has its own individual scent.

conkeldurr.description: When going all out, this Pokémon throws aside its concrete pillars and leaps at opponents to pummel them with its fists.

copperajah.description: These Pokémon live in herds. Their trunks have incredible grip strength, strong enough to crush giant rocks into powder.

corphish.description: It was originally a Pokémon from afar that escaped to the wild. It can adapt to the dirtiest river.

corsola.description: These Pokémon live in warm seas. In prehistoric times, many lived in the oceans around the Galar region as well.

corviknight.description: With their great intellect and flying skills, these Pokémon very successfully act as the Galar region’s airborne taxi service.

corvisquire.description: The lessons of many harsh battles have taught it how to accurately judge an opponent’s strength.

cosmoem.description: It sucks in dust from the air at an astounding rate, frantically building up energy within its core as preparation for evolution.

cosmog.description: Cosmog is very curious but not very cautious, often placing itself in danger. If things start to look dicey, it teleports away.

cottonee.description: Weaving together the cotton of both Cottonee and Eldegoss produces exquisite cloth that’s highly prized by many luxury brands.

crabominable.description: Before it stops to think, it just starts pummeling. There are records of its turning back avalanches with a flurry of punches.

crabrawler.description: Crabrawler has been known to mistake Exeggutor for a coconut tree and climb it. The enraged Exeggutor shakes it off and stomps it.

cradily.description: Once Cradily catches prey in its tentacles, it digests them whole and absorbs their nutrients.

cramorant.description: This hungry Pokémon swallows Arrokuda whole. Occasionally, it makes a mistake and tries to swallow a Pokémon other than its preferred prey.

cranidos.description: An incredibly rare sight. They duel each other by ramming their heads together, and the resulting sound echoes throughout the area like the pealing of a bell.

crawdaunt.description: A brutish Pokémon that loves to battle. It will crash itself into any foe that approaches its nest.

cresselia.description: Cresselia is reminiscent of the crescent moon. It leaves a brilliant line of light in its wake as it flies across the night sky. I daresay it resembles the heavenly maiden who created the Milky Way.

croagunk.description: A poison wielder with a dastardly personality. Despite such qualities, this species is afforded a measure of popularity due to its peculiar cry and comical features.

crobat.description: Its hind limbs have become another set of wings. Crobat expertly maneuvers its four wings to dart in exquisite fashion through even the most confined caves without losing any speed.

crocalor.description: The valve in Crocalor’s flame sac is closely connected to its vocal cords. This Pokémon utters a guttural cry as it spews flames every which way.

croconaw.description: Once Croconaw has clamped its jaws on its foe, it will absolutely not let go. Because the tips of its fangs are forked back like barbed fishhooks, they become impossible to remove when they have sunk in.

crustle.description: Its thick claws are its greatest weapons. They’re mighty enough to crack Rhyperior’s carapace.

cryogonal.description: When the weather gets hot, these Pokémon turn into water vapor. Cryogonal are almost never seen during summer.

cubchoo.description: It sniffles before performing a move, using its frosty snot to provide an icy element to any move that needs it.

cubone.description: This Pokémon wears the skull of its deceased mother. Sometimes Cubone’s dreams make it cry, but each tear Cubone sheds makes it stronger.

cufant.description: If a job requires serious strength, this Pokémon will excel at it. Its copper body tarnishes in the rain, turning a vibrant green color.

cursola.description: Be cautious of the ectoplasmic body surrounding its soul. You’ll become stiff as stone if you touch it.

cutiefly.description: An opponent’s aura can tell Cutiefly what that opponent’s next move will be. Then Cutiefly can glide around the attack and strike back.

cyclizar.description: It can sprint at over 70 mph while carrying a human. The rider’s body heat warms Cyclizar’s back and lifts the Pokémon’s spirit.

cyndaquil.description: Hails from the Johto region. Though usually curled into a ball due to its timid disposition, it harbors tremendous firepower.

dachsbun.description: The surface of this Pokémon’s skin hardens when exposed to intense heat, and its body has an appetizing aroma.

darkrai.description: On a moonless night, a strange incident occurred in which every one of a village's inhabitants suffered nightmares. The villagers attested that Darkrai appeared before them in these nightmares.

darmanitan-standard.description: This Pokémon’s power level rises along with the temperature of its fire, which can reach 2,500 degrees Fahrenheit.

dartrix.description: Regularly basks in sunlight to gather power—presumably due to the frigid climate. Nonetheless, the edges of the blade quills set into its wings are keen as ever.

darumaka.description: This popular symbol of good fortune will never fall over in its sleep, no matter how it’s pushed or pulled.

decidueye.description: The air stored inside the rachises of Decidueye's feathers insulates the Pokémon against Hisui's extreme cold. This is firm proof that evolution can be influenced by environment.

dedenne.description: Since Dedenne can’t generate much electricity on its own, it steals electricity from outlets or other electric Pokémon.

deerling.description: The turning of the seasons changes the color and scent of this Pokémon’s fur. People use it to mark the seasons.

deino.description: Because it can’t see, this Pokémon is constantly biting at everything it touches, trying to keep track of its surroundings.

delcatty.description: Delcatty sleeps anywhere it wants without keeping a permanent nest. If other Pokémon approach it as it sleeps, this Pokémon will never fight—it will just move away somewhere else.

delibird.description: It has a generous habit of sharing its food with people and Pokémon, so it’s always scrounging around for more food.

delphox.description: Using psychic power, it generates a fiery vortex of 5,400 degrees Fahrenheit, incinerating foes swept into this whirl of flame.

deoxys-normal.description: Deoxys emerged from a virus that came from space. It is highly intelligent and wields psychokinetic powers. This Pokémon shoots lasers from the crystalline organ on its chest.

dewgong.description: Its entire body is a snowy white. Unharmed by even intense cold, it swims powerfully in icy waters.

dewott.description: Its exquisite double-scalchop technique is likely the result of daily training, and it can send even masters of the blade fleeing in defeat.

dewpider.description: Dewpider normally lives underwater. When it comes onto land in search of food, it takes water with it in the form of a bubble on its head.

dhelmise.description: After lowering its anchor, it waits for its prey. It catches large Wailord and drains their life-force.

dialga.description: This Pokémon is revered as a deity in Hisuian legend. The birth of Dialga was what caused the vast river of time to begin flowing in our world.

diancie.description: It can instantly create many diamonds by compressing the carbon in the air between its hands.

diggersby.description: The fur on its belly retains heat exceptionally well. People used to make heavy winter clothing from fur shed by this Pokémon.

diglett.description: It burrows through the ground at a shallow depth. It leaves raised earth in its wake, making it easy to spot.

dipplin.description: The head sticking out belongs to the fore-wyrm, while the tail belongs to the core-wyrm. The two share one apple and help each other out.

ditto.description: When it encounters another Ditto, it will move faster than normal to duplicate that opponent exactly.

dodrio.description: One of Doduo’s two heads splits to form a unique species. It runs close to 40 mph in prairies.

doduo.description: Its short wings make flying difficult. Instead, this Pokémon runs at high speed on developed legs.

dolliv.description: It basks in the sun to its heart’s content until the fruits on its head ripen. After that, Dolliv departs from human settlements and goes on a journey.

dondozo.description: It treats Tatsugiri like its boss and follows it loyally. Though powerful, Dondozo is apparently not very smart.

donphan.description: If Donphan were to tackle with its hard body, even a house could be destroyed. Using its massive strength, the Pokémon helps clear rock and mud slides that block mountain trails.

dottler.description: As it grows inside its shell, it uses its psychic abilities to monitor the outside world and prepare for evolution.

doublade.description: The two swords employ a strategy of rapidly alternating between offense and defense to bring down their prey.

dracovish.description: Its mighty legs are capable of running at speeds exceeding 40 mph, but this Pokémon can’t breathe unless it’s underwater.

dracozolt.description: The powerful muscles in its tail generate its electricity. Compared to its lower body, its upper half is entirely too small.

dragalge.description: Dragalge generates dragon energy by sticking the plume on its head out above the ocean’s surface and bathing it in sunlight.

dragapult.description: Apparently the Dreepy inside Dragapult’s horns eagerly look forward to being launched out at Mach speeds.

dragonair.description: This Pokémon gathers power in the orbs on its tail and controls the weather. When enshrouded by an aura, Dragonair has a mystical appearance.

dragonite.description: This Pokémon is known as the Sea Incarnate. Figureheads that resemble Dragonite decorate the bows of many ships.

drakloak.description: Without a Dreepy to place on its head and care for, it gets so uneasy it’ll try to substitute any Pokémon it finds for the missing Dreepy.

drampa.description: Drampa is a kind and friendly Pokémon—up until it’s angered. When that happens, it stirs up a gale and flattens everything around.

drapion.description: Has a brutish, ferocious temperament. With immense strength and a sturdy shell off which swords will bounce, it rampages about and wreaks havoc.

dratini.description: This Pokémon was long considered to be no more than a myth. The small lump on a Dratini’s forehead is actually a horn that’s still coming in.

drednaw.description: This Pokémon rapidly extends its retractable neck to sink its sharp fangs into distant enemies and take them down.

dreepy.description: If this weak Pokémon is by itself, a mere child could defeat it. But if Dreepy has friends to help it train, it can evolve and become much stronger.

drifblim.description: It drifts along at dusk, perfectly silent. Its transient, melancholy aspect touches some people deeply—every so often, one will come upon a song or poem devoted to Drifblim.

drifloon.description: Said to lure away young children and carry them off to the afterlife. Some whisper that Drifloon are formed of reincarnated human souls, but these rumors are as yet unconfirmed.

drilbur.description: It’s a digger, using its claws to burrow through the ground. It causes damage to vegetable crops, so many farmers have little love for it.

drizzile.description: Highly intelligent but also very lazy, it keeps enemies out of its territory by laying traps everywhere.

drowzee.description: If you sleep by it all the time, it will sometimes show you dreams it had eaten in the past.

druddigon.description: Druddigon are vicious and cunning. They take up residence in nests dug out by other Pokémon, treating the stolen nests as their own lairs.

dubwool.description: Its majestic horns are meant only to impress the opposite gender. They never see use in battle.

ducklett.description: They are better at swimming than flying, and they happily eat their favorite food, peat moss, as they dive underwater.

dudunsparce-two-segment.description: It drives enemies out of its nest by sucking in enough air to fill its long, narrow lungs, then releasing the air in an intense blast.

dugtrio.description: These Diglett triplets dig over 60 miles below sea level. No one knows what it’s like underground.

dunsparce.description: The nests Dunsparce live in are mazes of tunnels. They never get lost in their own nests—they can tell where they are by the scent of the dirt.

duosion.description: Its brain has split into two, and the two halves rarely think alike. Its actions are utterly unpredictable.

duraludon.description: The special metal that composes its body is very light, so this Pokémon has considerable agility. It lives in caves because it dislikes the rain.

durant.description: With their large mandibles, these Pokémon can crunch their way through rock. They work together to protect their eggs from Sandaconda.

dusclops.description: There are rumors that peeking inside its bandage-wrapped body will cause one to get pulled in through the gaps between the bandages, never to return. I've been too scared to verify.

dusknoir.description: Comes to those whose lives have come to an end and escorts their souls to the afterlife. Known to mistakenly take the souls of those who yet have life left in them, albeit rarely.

duskull.description: I've heard that the children of Hisui all begin to behave once they've been told the story of how this Pokémon roams about before the witching hour to spirit away misbehaving children.

dustox.description: Tends to be drawn to bonfires on dark nights. Difficult to chase away from settlements because of the way it scatters highly toxic scales.

dwebble.description: It first tries to find a rock to live in, but if there are no suitable rocks to be found, Dwebble may move in to the ports of a Hippowdon.

eelektrik.description: These Pokémon have a big appetite. When they spot their prey, they attack it and paralyze it with electricity.

eelektross.description: They crawl out of the ocean using their arms. They will attack prey on shore and immediately drag it into the ocean.

eevee.description: Harbors the potential to evolve into manifold forms. Within Eevee lies the key to the mysteries of Pokémon evolution—I'm certain of it.

eiscue-ice.description: This Pokémon keeps its heat-sensitive head cool with ice. It fishes for its food, dangling its single hair into the sea to lure in prey.

ekans.description: The older it gets, the longer it grows. At night, it wraps its long body around tree branches to rest.

eldegoss.description: The cotton on the head of this Pokémon can be spun into a glossy, gorgeous yarn—a Galar regional specialty.

electabuzz.description: Feeds on electrical energy. During sudden showers beneath looming thunderclouds, one can observe Electabuzz scaling tall trees, where the Pokémon will then wait for lightning to strike.

electivire.description: Its evolution was induced by an unusual item, and its electrical output rises along with its heart rate. From its tails, it can unleash an electric current measuring 20,000 volts.

electrike.description: It stores electricity in its fur. It gives off sparks from all over its body in seasons when the air is dry.

electrode.description: The tissue on the surface of its body is curiously similar in composition to an Apricorn. When irritated, this Pokémon lets loose an electric current equal to 20 lightning bolts.

elekid.description: They generate electricity by spinning their arms. During a thunderstorm, if one hears the lively voices of children out in the wilderness, what one is actually hearing are the voices of Elekid.

elgyem.description: This Pokémon was discovered about 50 years ago. Its highly developed brain enables it to exert its psychic powers.

emboar.description: It has mastered fast and powerful fighting moves. It grows a beard of fire.

emolga.description: This Pokémon absolutely loves sweet berries. Sometimes it stuffs its cheeks full of so much food that it can’t fly properly.

empoleon.description: Since ancient times, it has been revered by the people of Hisui, who call it the Master of the Waves. Its wings are a match for even master-crafted blades.

enamorus-incarnate.description: When it flies to this land from across the sea, the bitter winter comes to an end. According to legend, this Pokémon's love gives rise to the budding of fresh life across Hisui.

entei.description: Entei embodies the passion of magma. This Pokémon is thought to have been born in the eruption of a volcano. It sends up massive bursts of fire that utterly consume all that they touch.

escavalier.description: It charges its enemies, lances at the ready. An image of one of its duels is captured in a famous painting of Escavalier clashing with Sirfetch’d.

espathra.description: It emits psychic power from the gaps between its multicolored frills and sprints at speeds greater than 120 mph.

espeon.description: Wields an arcane power with which it can predict the weather and even people's thoughts. When bathed in sunshine, the scarlet orb on its brow glows and builds energy.

espurr.description: There’s enough psychic power in Espurr to send a wrestler flying, but because this power can’t be controlled, Espurr finds it troublesome.

eternatus.description: It was inside a meteorite that fell 20,000 years ago. There seems to be a connection between this Pokémon and the Dynamax phenomenon.

excadrill.description: Known as the Drill King, this Pokémon can tunnel through the terrain at speeds of over 90 mph.

exeggcute.description: These Pokémon get nervous when they’re not in a group of six. The minute even one member of the group goes missing, Exeggcute become cowardly.

exeggutor.description: When they work together, Exeggutor’s three heads can put out powerful psychic energy. Cloudy days make this Pokémon sluggish.

exploud.description: This Pokémon can do more than just shout. To communicate with others of its kind, it’ll emit all sorts of sounds from the holes in its body.

falinks.description: The six of them work together as one Pokémon. Teamwork is also their battle strategy, and they constantly change their formation as they fight.

farfetchd.description: They use a plant stalk as a weapon, but not all of them use it in the same way. Several distinct styles of stalk fighting have been observed.

farigiraf.description: The hardened head from the tail protects the head of the main body as Farigiraf whips its long neck around to headbutt enemies.

fearow.description: A Pokémon that dates back many years. If it senses danger, it flies high and away, instantly.

feebas.description: It is a shabby and ugly Pokémon. However, it is very hardy and can survive on little water.

fennekin.description: As it walks, it munches on a twig in place of a snack. It intimidates opponents by puffing hot air out of its ears.

feraligatr.description: Feraligatr intimidates its foes by opening its huge mouth. In battle, it will kick the ground hard with its thick and powerful hind legs to charge at the foe at an incredible speed.

ferroseed.description: Mossy caves are their preferred dwellings. Enzymes contained in mosses help Ferroseed’s spikes grow big and strong.

ferrothorn.description: Its spikes are harder than steel. This Pokémon crawls across rock walls by stabbing the spikes on its feelers into the stone.

fezandipiti.description: Fezandipiti beats its glossy wings to scatter pheromones that captivate people and Pokémon.

fidough.description: The yeast in Fidough’s breath is useful for cooking, so this Pokémon has been protected by people since long ago.

finizen.description: Its water ring is made from seawater mixed with a sticky fluid that Finizen secretes from its blowhole.

finneon.description: What a gorgeous sight this Pokémon is as it swims with its long, pink-painted caudal fins fluttering behind it. Finneon's beautiful appearance has led to its nickname: ”finery fish.”

flaaffy.description: It stores electricity in its fluffy fleece. If it stores up too much, it will start to go bald in those patches.

flabebe.description: Flabébé wears a crown made from pollen it’s collected from its flower. The crown has hidden healing properties.

flamigo.description: Thanks to a behavior of theirs known as “synchronizing,” an entire flock of these Pokémon can attack simultaneously in perfect harmony.

flapple.description: It flies on wings of apple skin and spits a powerful acid. It can also change its shape into that of an apple.

flareon.description: Flames burn within a saclike organ inside this Pokémon. When Flareon inhales, these flames grow in intensity, reaching a mighty 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit.

fletchinder.description: Fletchinder are exceedingly territorial and aggressive. These Pokémon fight among themselves over feeding grounds.

fletchling.description: When this Pokémon gets excited, its body temperature increases sharply. If you touch a Fletchling with bare hands, you might get burned.

flittle.description: It spends its time running around wastelands. If anyone steals its beloved berries, it will chase them down and exact its revenge.

floatzel.description: Has a long, rather splendid flotation sac, which prevents Floatzel from drowning even in stormy seas. One might glimpse this species around fishing hamlets from time to time.

floette.description: It gives its own power to flowers, pouring its heart into caring for them. Floette never forgives anyone who messes up a flower bed.

floragato.description: The hardness of Floragato’s fur depends on the Pokémon’s mood. When Floragato is prepared to battle, its fur becomes pointed and needle sharp.

florges.description: Its life can span several hundred years. It’s said to devote its entire life to protecting gardens.

flutter-mane.description: It has similar features to a ghostly pterosaur that was covered in a paranormal magazine, but the two have little else in common.

flygon.description: It is nicknamed the Desert Spirit because the flapping of its wings sounds like a woman singing.

fomantis.description: During the day, Fomantis basks in sunlight and sleeps peacefully. It wakes and moves around at night.

foongus.description: The spores released from this Pokémon’s hands are highly poisonous, but when thoroughly dried, the spores can be used as stomach medicine.

forretress.description: In the moment that it gulps down its prey, the inside of its shell is exposed, but to this day, no one has ever seen that sight.

fraxure.description: Its skin is as hard as a suit of armor. Fraxure’s favorite strategy is to tackle its opponents, stabbing them with its tusks at the same time.

frigibax.description: This Pokémon lives in forests and craggy areas. Using the power of its dorsal fin, it cools the inside of its nest like a refrigerator.

frillish-male.description: Legend has it that the residents of a sunken ancient city changed into these Pokémon.

froakie.description: It protects its skin by covering its body in delicate bubbles. Beneath its happy-go-lucky air, it keeps a watchful eye on its surroundings.

frogadier.description: Its swiftness is unparalleled. It can scale a tower of more than 2,000 feet in a minute’s time.

froslass.description: A Pokémon inhabited by the soul of a woman who died bearing a grudge in the snowy mountains. Legends of Froslass placing deathly curses on misbehaving men send shivers down my spine.

frosmoth.description: It shows no mercy to any who desecrate fields and mountains. It will fly around on its icy wings, causing a blizzard to chase offenders away.

fuecoco.description: Its flame sac is small, so energy is always leaking out. This energy is released from the dent atop Fuecoco’s head and flickers to and fro.

furfrou.description: Left alone, its fur will grow longer and longer, but it will only allow someone it trusts to cut it.

furret.description: Furret has a very slim build. When under attack, it can slickly squirm through narrow spaces and get away. In spite of its short limbs, this Pokémon is very nimble and fleet.

gabite.description: Though Gabite are usually of a violent disposition, when I gave one a glass bead it had been eyeing covetously, it suddenly became quite docile.

gallade.description: The blades extending from its elbows are sharper than the finest swords. Its swordsmanship, albeit self-taught, is astonishingly impressive.

galvantula.description: It lays traps of electrified threads near the nests of bird Pokémon, aiming to snare chicks that are not yet good at flying.

garbodor.description: The toxic liquid it launches from its right arm is so virulent that it can kill a weakened creature instantly.

garchomp.description: Soars across the heavens at blinding speed—a magnificent sight! It has a feral disposition. Utmost caution is required if one meets a Garchomp out in the wilds.

gardevoir.description: It will dedicate itself to defending a master it has come to adore. Its pure white dress, reminiscent of those worn by ladies of nobility, is the dress of one who is willing to risk their life.

garganacl.description: Many Pokémon gather around Garganacl, hoping to lick at its mineral-rich salt.

gastly.description: Gaseous and completely impalpable. Also highly dangerous— inhaling part of its poisonous body will cause one to faint instantly.

gastrodon.description: Eats beach sand for nourishment. Should one Gastrodon encounter another of a different color, a fierce battle will inevitably ensue.

genesect.description: This Pokémon existed 300 million years ago. Team Plasma altered it and attached a cannon to its back.

gengar.description: Possesses potential victims' shadows in an effort to steal away the victims' lives. If your shadow begins to laugh, you must take hold of a protective charm posthaste!

geodude.description: Makes its home in mountainous regions, using its arms to climb along harsh mountain roads. Can be troublesome—carelessly kicking one will cause it to fly into a rage and chase after you.

gholdengo.description: It has a sturdy body made up of stacked coins. Gholdengo overwhelms its enemies by firing coin after coin at them in quick succession.

gible.description: It nests in caves untouched by sunlight. Its sharp teeth may fall out when worn away or after an impact, but they regrow within a few days.

gigalith.description: Although its energy blasts can blow away a dump truck, they have a limitation— they can only be fired when the sun is out.

gimmighoul.description: It lives inside an old treasure chest. Sometimes it gets left in shop corners since no one realizes it’s actually a Pokémon.

girafarig.description: Girafarig’s rear head contains a tiny brain that is too small for thinking. However, the rear head doesn’t need to sleep, so it can keep watch over its surroundings 24 hours a day.

giratina-altered.description: There is one Hisuian verse that tells of a powerful light creating a deep shadow. I imagine that this deep shadow is Giratina.

glaceon.description: Glaceon is able to lower its body temperature very quickly. It freezes the atmosphere, creating diamond dust that glitters like gems while it flutters and dances around.

glalie.description: It covers its body with an armor of ice harder than steel. Uses its breath to freeze prey, which it then devours as if they were frozen desserts.

glameow.description: Bewitches humans with its helical tail and piercing gaze. Its hidden claws are quite sharp as well, making this Pokémon an exceedingly tricky opponent if antagonized.

glastrier.description: Glastrier has tremendous physical strength, and the mask of ice covering its face is 100 times harder than diamond.

gligar.description: Its tail is tipped by a thick, horrible stinger. To bring down prey, it will first obscure their vision by covering their faces with its body, and then it will use the stinger to inject them with venom.

glimmet.description: Glimmet’s toxic mineral crystals look just like flower petals. This Pokémon scatters poisonous powder like pollen to protect itself.

glimmora.description: Glimmora’s petals are made of crystallized poison energy. It has recently become evident that these petals resemble Tera Jewels.

gliscor.description: It glides soundlessly on pitch-black wings and sinks sharp fangs into the throat of its prey. It takes on a look of satisfaction once it has entirely drained its prey of blood.

gloom.description: What appears to be drool is actually sweet honey. It is very sticky and clings stubbornly if touched.

gogoat.description: They inhabit mountainous regions. The leader of the herd is decided by a battle of clashing horns.

golbat.description: It sinks its sharp fangs into other creatures and slurps up their blood. A closer look at the fangs reveals that they are hollow and akin to straws.

goldeen.description: Its dorsal and pectoral fins are strongly developed like muscles. It can swim at a speed of five knots.

golduck.description: Its body is strong, and it has webbing on its hands and feet. Golduck can swim easily through rough seas, clawing its way through the high waves.

golem.description: The rocklike shell is shed each year. The cast-off shell then crumbles, reverting to a mass of soil, which can be spread across fields to promote crop growth.

golett.description: This Pokémon was created from clay. It received orders from its master many thousands of years ago, and it still follows those orders to this day.

golisopod.description: They live in sunken ships or in holes in the seabed. When Golisopod and Grapploct battle, the loser becomes the winner’s meal.

golurk.description: There’s a theory that inside Golurk is a perpetual motion machine that produces limitless energy, but this belief hasn’t been proven.

goodra.description: Able to freely control the hardness of its metallic shell. It loathes solitude and is extremely clingy—it will fume and run riot if those dearest to it ever leave its side.

goomy.description: Goomy hides away in the shade of trees, where it's nice and humid. If the slime coating its body dries out, the Pokémon instantly becomes lethargic.

gorebyss.description: It sucks bodily fluids out of its prey. The leftover meat sinks to the seafloor, where it becomes food for other Pokémon.

gossifleur.description: It whirls around in the wind while singing a joyous song. This delightful display has charmed many into raising this Pokémon.

gothita.description: Even when nobody seems to be around, Gothita can still be heard making a muted cry. Many believe it’s speaking to something only it can see.

gothitelle.description: A criminal who was shown his fate by a Gothitelle went missing that same day and was never seen again.

gothorita.description: On nights when the stars shine, this Pokémon’s psychic power is at its strongest. It’s unknown just what link Gothorita has to the greater universe.

gouging-fire.description: It resembles an eerie Pokémon once shown in a paranormal magazine. That Pokémon was said to be an Entei regenerated from a fossil.

gourgeist-average.description: In the darkness of a new-moon night, Gourgeist will come knocking. Whoever answers the door will be swept off to the afterlife.

grafaiai.description: Each Grafaiai paints its own individual pattern, and it will paint that same pattern over and over again throughout its life.

granbull.description: Although it’s popular with young people, Granbull is timid and sensitive, so it’s totally incompetent as a watchdog.

grapploct.description: Searching for an opponent to test its skills against, it emerges onto land. Once the battle is over, it returns to the sea.

graveler.description: Dwells in holes dug into sheer walls of stone. It enjoys rolling down slopes as though it were a boulder during a rockfall, so keep an eye upward while traversing mountain roads.

great-tusk.description: This creature resembles a mysterious Pokémon that, according to a paranormal magazine, has lived since ancient times.

greavard.description: This friendly Pokémon doesn’t like being alone. Pay it even the slightest bit of attention, and it will follow you forever.

greedent.description: Common throughout the Galar region, this Pokémon has strong teeth and can chew through the toughest of berry shells.

greninja.description: It appears and vanishes with a ninja’s grace. It toys with its enemies using swift movements, while slicing them with throwing stars of sharpest water.

grimer.description: Made of congealed sludge. It smells too putrid to touch. Even weeds won’t grow in its path.

grimmsnarl.description: Its hairs work like muscle fibers. When its hairs unfurl, they latch on to opponents, ensnaring them as tentacles would.

grookey.description: It attacks with rapid beats of its stick. As it strikes with amazing speed, it gets more and more pumped.

grotle.description: Appears where there is clean spring water. The fruit that grows on the shrubs on its shell is sweet, nutritious, and truly delicious.

groudon.description: Through Primal Reversion and with nature’s full power, it will take back its true form. It can cause magma to erupt and expand the landmass of the world.

grovyle.description: This Pokémon adeptly flies from branch to branch in trees. In a forest, no Pokémon can ever hope to catch a fleeing Grovyle however fast they may be.

growlithe.description: They patrol their territory in pairs. I believe the igneous rock components in the fur of this species are the result of volcanic activity in its habitat.

grubbin.description: It uses its big jaws to dig nests into the forest floor, and it loves to feed on sweet tree sap.

grumpig.description: Grumpig uses the black pearls on its body to wield its fantastic powers. When it is doing so, it dances bizarrely. This Pokémon’s black pearls are valuable as works of art.

gulpin.description: Most of Gulpin’s body is made up of its stomach—its heart and brain are very small in comparison. This Pokémon’s stomach contains special enzymes that dissolve anything.

gumshoos.description: Patient by nature, this Pokémon loses control of itself and pounces when it spots its favorite meal—Rattata!

gurdurr.description: Gurdurr excels at demolition—construction is not its forte. In any case, there’s skill in the way this Pokémon wields its metal beam.

guzzlord.description: An unknown life-form called a UB. It may be constantly hungry—it is certainly always devouring something.

gyarados.description: I suspect this Pokémon to be the true identity of a dragon written of in ancient texts, which claimed that it razed an entire village with white-hot beams from its maw.

hakamo-o.description: Before attacking its enemies, it clashes its scales together and roars. Its sharp claws shred the opposition.

happiny.description: In imitation of Chansey, it keeps a round stone tucked into its belly pouch and cherishes it dearly. It gets along well with children and will sometimes play house with them for fun.

hariyama.description: Hariyama that are big and fat aren’t necessarily strong. There are some small ones that move nimbly and use moves skillfully.

hatenna.description: If this Pokémon senses a strong emotion, it will run away as fast as it can. It prefers areas without people.

hatterene.description: If you’re too loud around it, you risk being torn apart by the claws on its tentacle. This Pokémon is also known as the Forest Witch.

hattrem.description: Using the braids on its head, it pummels foes to get them to quiet down. One blow from those braids would knock out a professional boxer.

haunter.description: This frightful, malevolent spirit can glide through walls, appearing wherever it likes. According to rumor, victims of a Haunter's lick will wither to death day by day.

hawlucha.description: It always strikes a pose before going for its finishing move. Sometimes opponents take advantage of that time to counterattack.

haxorus.description: While usually kindhearted, it can be terrifying if angered. Tusks that can slice through steel beams are how Haxorus deals with its adversaries.

heatmor.description: A flame serves as its tongue, melting through the hard shell of Durant so that Heatmor can devour their insides.

heatran.description: Stories tell of this Pokémon being birthed from the boiling magma within Mount Coronet. Its molten-steel body holds many mysteries.

heliolisk.description: One Heliolisk basking in the sun with its frill outspread is all it would take to produce enough electricity to power a city.

helioptile.description: The sun powers this Pokémon’s electricity generation. Interruption of that process stresses Helioptile to the point of weakness.

heracross.description: This Pokémon has an unparalleled horn. Heracross itself demonstrates tremendous power—it's capable of throwing several people trained in the traditional arts of war at once.

herdier.description: The black fur that covers this Pokémon’s body is dense and springy. Even sharp fangs bounce right off.

hippopotas.description: Though large and languid, Hippopotas is difficult to detect due to its tendency to burrow into and lurk beneath the soil. When agitated or excited, it expels sand from its nostrils.

hippowdon.description: Short-tempered and easily moved to violence. It whips up whirlwinds of sand to crush its foes' spirits, then goes in for the attack.

hitmonchan.description: Its punches slice the air. However, it seems to need a short break after fighting for three minutes.

hitmonlee.description: The legs freely contract and stretch. The stretchy legs allow it to hit a distant foe with a rising kick.

hitmontop.description: After doing a handstand to throw off the opponent’s timing, it presents its fancy kick moves.

ho-oh.description: Ho-Oh’s feathers glow in seven colors depending on the angle at which they are struck by light. These feathers are said to bring happiness to the bearers. This Pokémon is said to live at the foot of a rainbow.

honchkrow.description: One cry from this Pokémon, and a murder of Murkrow come flying. At such times, one would think the curtain of night had fallen, plunging the world into jet-black darkness.

honedge.description: The blue eye on the sword’s handguard is the true body of Honedge. With its old cloth, it drains people’s lives away.

hoopa.description: It is said to be able to seize anything it desires with its six rings and six huge arms. With its power sealed, it is transformed into a much smaller form.

hoothoot.description: It begins to hoot at the same time every day. Some Trainers use them in place of clocks.

hoppip.description: This Pokémon drifts and floats with the wind. If it senses the approach of strong winds, Hoppip links its leaves with other Hoppip to prepare against being blown away.

horsea.description: They swim with dance-like motions and cause whirlpools to form. Horsea compete to see which of them can generate the biggest whirlpool.

houndoom.description: Identifiable by its eerie howls, people a long time ago thought it was the grim reaper and feared it.

houndour.description: They make repeated eerie howls before dawn to call attention to their pack.

houndstone.description: A lovingly mourned Pokémon was reborn as Houndstone. It doesn’t like anyone touching the protuberance atop its head.

huntail.description: Deep seas are their habitat. According to tradition, when Huntail wash up onshore, something unfortunate will happen.

hydrapple.description: These capricious syrpents have banded together. On the rare occasion that their moods align, their true power is unleashed.

hydreigon.description: The three heads take turns sinking their teeth into the opponent. Their attacks won’t slow until their target goes down.

hypno.description: Avoid eye contact if you come across one. It will try to put you to sleep by using its pendulum.

igglybuff.description: Taking advantage of the softness of its body, Igglybuff moves as if bouncing. Its body turns a deep pink when its temperature rises.

illumise.description: Illumise leads a flight of illuminated Volbeat to draw signs in the night sky. This Pokémon is said to earn greater respect from its peers by composing more complex designs in the sky.

impidimp.description: It sneaks into people’s homes, stealing things and feasting on the negative energy of the frustrated occupants.

incineroar.description: Incineroar’s rough and aggressive behavior is its most notable trait, but the way it helps out small Pokémon shows that it has a kind side as well.

indeedee-male.description: Through its horns, it can pick up on the emotions of creatures around it. Positive emotions are the source of its strength.

infernape.description: A tall, hardy Pokémon with a dazzling appearance. It shrouds itself in flame and battles as if engaged in dance—truly a sight to behold.

inkay.description: By exposing foes to the blinking of its luminescent spots, Inkay demoralizes them, and then it seizes the chance to flee.

inteleon.description: Its nictitating membranes let it pick out foes’ weak points so it can precisely blast them with water that shoots from its fingertips at Mach 3.

iron-boulder.description: It was named after a mysterious object recorded in an old book. Its body seems to be metallic.

iron-bundle.description: It resembles a mysterious object mentioned in an old book. There are only two reported sightings of this Pokémon.

iron-crown.description: There was supposedly an incident in which it launched shining blades to cut everything around it to pieces. Little else is known about it.

iron-hands.description: This Pokémon shares many similarities with Iron Hands, an object mentioned in a certain expedition journal.

iron-jugulis.description: It’s possible that Iron Jugulis, an object described in an old book, may actually be this Pokémon.

iron-leaves.description: According to the few eyewitness accounts that exist, it used its shining blades to julienne large trees and boulders.

iron-moth.description: No records exist of this species being caught. Data is lacking, but the Pokémon’s traits match up with an object described in an old book.

iron-thorns.description: Some of its notable features match those of an object named within a certain expedition journal as Iron Thorns.

iron-treads.description: Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. It resembles a mysterious object described in an old expedition journal.

iron-valiant.description: It’s possible that this is the object listed as Iron Valiant in a certain expedition journal.

ivysaur.description: Exposure to sunlight adds to its strength. Sunlight also makes the bud on its back grow larger.

jangmo-o.description: Jangmo-o strikes its scales to communicate with others of its kind. Its scales are actually fur that’s become as hard as metal.

jellicent-male.description: Whenever a full moon hangs in the night sky, schools of Jellicent gather near the surface of the sea, waiting for their prey to appear.

jigglypuff.description: By freely changing the wavelength of its voice, Jigglypuff sings a mysterious melody sure to make any listener sleepy.

jirachi.description: It’s believed that when this Pokémon wakes from its 1,000-year slumber, it will grant any wishes written on the notes attached to its head.

jolteon.description: Bristles its fur into sharp, needlelike points when enraged. One can hear electricity crackle in its breath when it exhales.

joltik.description: Joltik latch on to other Pokémon and suck out static electricity. They’re often found sticking to Yamper’s hindquarters.

jumpluff.description: Jumpluff rides warm southern winds to cross the sea and fly to foreign lands. The Pokémon descends to the ground when it encounters cold air while it is floating.

jynx.description: The Jynx of Galar often have beautiful and delicate voices. Some of these Pokémon have even gathered a fan base.

kabuto.description: While some say this species has gone extinct, Kabuto sightings are apparently fairly common in some places.

kabutops.description: The cause behind the extinction of this species is unknown. Kabutops were aggressive Pokémon that inhabited warm seas.

kadabra.description: There are rumors that a child with mystical powers became a Kadabra; however, this remains unverified. I suspect that the spoon Kadabra holds enhances its brain waves.

kakuna.description: Able to move only slightly. When endangered, it may stick out its stinger and poison its enemy.

kangaskhan.description: There are records of a lost human child being raised by a childless Kangaskhan.

karrablast.description: It spits a liquid from its mouth to melt through Shelmet’s shell. Karrablast doesn’t eat the shell— it eats only the contents.

kartana.description: Although it’s alien to this world and a danger here, it’s apparently a common organism in the world where it normally lives.

kecleon.description: Its color changes for concealment and also when its mood or health changes. The darker the color, the healthier it is.

keldeo-ordinary.description: They say that Keldeo must survive harsh battles and fully develop the horn on its forehead before this Pokémon’s true power will awaken.

kilowattrel.description: It uses its throat sac to store electricity generated by its wings. There’s hardly any oil in its feathers, so it is a poor swimmer.

kingambit.description: Though it commands a massive army in battle, it’s not skilled at devising complex strategies. It just uses brute strength to keep pushing.

kingdra.description: Scales shed by this Pokémon have such a splendorous gleam to them that they’ve been given to royalty as gifts.

kingler.description: Its oversized claw is very powerful, but when it’s not in battle, the claw just gets in the way.

kirlia.description: It resembles a maiden in appearance, but it wields strange powers to project visions of paradise. I suspect the crimson ornaments on its head are the key to its abilities.

klang.description: Many companies in the Galar region choose Klang as their logo. This Pokémon is considered the symbol of industrial technology.

klawf.description: This Pokémon lives on sheer cliffs. It sidesteps opponents’ attacks, then lunges for their weak spots with its claws.

kleavor.description: A violent creature that fells towering trees with its crude axes and shields itself with hard stone. If one should chance upon this Pokémon in the wilds, one's only recourse is to flee.

klefki.description: Klefki sucks in metal ions with the horn topping its head. It seems this Pokémon loves keys so much that its head needed to look like one, too.

klink.description: It’s suspected that Klink were the inspiration behind ancient people’s invention of the first gears.

klinklang.description: The three gears that compose this Pokémon spin at high speed. Its new spiked gear isn’t a living creature.

koffing.description: It adores polluted air. Some claim that Koffing used to be more plentiful in the Galar region than they are now.

komala.description: It remains asleep from birth to death as a result of the sedative properties of the leaves that form its diet.

kommo-o.description: Certain ruins have paintings of ancient warriors wearing armor made of Kommo-o scales.

koraidon.description: This Pokémon resembles Cyclizar, but it is far burlier and more ferocious. Nothing is known about its ecology or other features.

krabby.description: If it senses danger approaching, it cloaks itself with bubbles from its mouth so it will look bigger.

kricketot.description: When the trees take on new hues, more of these Pokémon appear. The tone they create by striking their antennae together resembles that of the marimba, an instrument of foreign lands.

kricketune.description: It uses its cutlass-like arms to produce sound, the melody of which varies from individual to individual. It is a worthwhile endeavor to seek out one's favorite tunes.

krokorok.description: Although this Pokémon has specialized eyes that allow it to see in the dark, Krokorok won’t move much at night—the desert gets cold after sunset.

krookodile.description: While terribly aggressive, Krookodile also has the patience to stay hidden under sand for days, lying in wait for prey.

kubfu.description: If Kubfu pulls the long white hair on its head, its fighting spirit heightens and power wells up from the depths of its belly.

kyogre.description: Kyogre is said to be the personification of the sea itself. Legends tell of its many clashes against Groudon, as each sought to gain the power of nature.

kyurem.description: It appears that this Pokémon uses its powers over ice to freeze its own body in order to stabilize its cellular structure.

lairon.description: During territorial disputes, Lairon fight by slamming into each other. Close inspection of their steel armor reveals scratches and dents.

lampent.description: It lurks in cities, pretending to be a lamp. Once it finds someone whose death is near, it will trail quietly after them.

landorus-incarnate.description: When the incarnations of wind and of lightning clash, Landorus arrives to quell the conflict. After the tempests and thunderbolts abate, the land is sure to be blessed with bountiful harvests.

lanturn.description: This Pokémon flashes a bright light that blinds its prey. This creates an opening for it to deliver an electrical attack.

lapras.description: Crossing icy seas is no issue for this cold-resistant Pokémon. Its smooth skin is a little cool to the touch.

larvesta.description: Larvesta’s body is warm all over. It spouts fire from the tips of its horns to intimidate predators and scare prey.

larvitar.description: It feeds on soil. After it has eaten a large mountain, it will fall asleep so it can grow.

latias.description: Latias is highly intelligent and capable of understanding human speech. It is covered with a glass-like down. The Pokémon enfolds its body with its down and refracts light to alter its appearance.

latios.description: Latios will only open its heart to a Trainer with a compassionate spirit. This Pokémon can fly faster than a jet plane by folding its forelegs to minimize air resistance.

leafeon.description: Cells similar to those of plants have been found in its fur. Its hard tail can fell a large tree with one stroke, and the tail's sharpness exceeds even that of a sword crafted by a master.

leavanny.description: It keeps its eggs warm with heat from fermenting leaves. It also uses leaves to make warm wrappings for Sewaddle.

lechonk.description: This Pokémon spurns all but the finest of foods. Its body gives off an herblike scent that bug Pokémon detest.

ledian.description: It flies through the night sky, sprinkling sparkly dust. According to some, if that dust sticks to you, good things will happen to you.

ledyba.description: These very cowardly Pokémon join together and use Reflect to protect their nest.

lickilicky.description: Its tongue can extend and contract freely, and it is capable of reaching lengths over 10 times Lickilicky's height. Beware of the saliva, as it contains corrosive elements.

lickitung.description: Wields its long tongue deftly, as though it were an arm. The Pokémon's viscous saliva, once it has been collected and boiled down, yields a strong and highly useful adhesive.

liepard.description: This stealthy Pokémon sneaks up behind prey without making any sound at all. It competes with Thievul for territory.

lileep.description: Lileep clings to rocks on the seabed. When prey comes close, this Pokémon entangles it with petallike tentacles.

lilligant.description: I suspect that its well-developed legs are the result of a life spent on mountains covered in deep snow. The scent it exudes from its flower crown heartens those in proximity.

lillipup.description: This Pokémon is far brighter than the average child, and Lillipup won’t forget the love it receives or any abuse it suffers.

linoone.description: It uses its explosive speed and razor-sharp claws to bring down prey. Running along winding paths is not its strong suit.

litleo.description: This hot-blooded Pokémon is filled with curiosity. When it gets angry or starts fighting, its short mane gets hot.

litten.description: Trying to pet Litten before it trusts you will result in a nasty scratch from its sharp claws. Be careful.

litwick.description: The younger the life this Pokémon absorbs, the brighter and eerier the flame on its head burns.

lokix.description: It uses its normally folded third set of legs when in Showdown Mode. This places a huge burden on its body, so it can’t stay in this mode for long.

lombre.description: It lives at the water’s edge where it is sunny. It sleeps on a bed of water grass by day and becomes active at night.

lopunny.description: Its fur is warm and yet remarkably light. This Pokémon kicks as though it were a master of karate, driving back its opponents with ease.

lotad.description: Its leaf grew too large for it to live on land. That is how it began to live floating in the water.

loudred.description: The force of this Pokémon’s loud voice isn’t just the sound—it’s also the wave of air pressure that blows opponents away and damages them.

lucario.description: A most gallant-looking creature. It emits energy waves and controls them with precision, using them to sense even faraway beings. I have given the name ”aura” to this power.

ludicolo.description: If it hears festive music, it begins moving in rhythm in order to amplify its power.

lugia.description: Lugia’s wings pack devastating power—a light fluttering of its wings can blow apart regular houses. As a result, this Pokémon chooses to live out of sight deep under the sea.

lumineon.description: Uses its gleaming fins to hunt its prey. The view of Lumineon schooling near the surface of the sea at night is breathtaking— it's as though there were shining stars right there.

lunala.description: It steals the light from its surroundings and then becomes the full moon, showering its own light across the night sky.

lunatone.description: It was discovered at the site of a meteor strike 40 years ago. Its stare can lull its foes to sleep.

lurantis.description: The petals on this Pokémon’s arms are thin and super sharp, and they can fire laser beams if Lurantis gathers light first.

luvdisc.description: Luvdisc makes its home in coral reefs in warm seas. It especially likes sleeping in the space between Corsola’s branches.

luxio.description: Proudly uses its electrified claws as weapons. It seems to be a gracious Pokémon, evenly sharing the spoils of the hunt with others of its kind.

luxray.description: They form packs, each having one male as leader. Legends say that when Luxray's two eyes shimmer with gold, the Pokémon can see through anything.

lycanroc-midday.description: With swift movements, this Pokémon gradually backs its prey into a corner. Lycanroc’s fangs are always aimed toward opponents’ weak spots.

mabosstiff.description: Mabosstiff loves playing with children. Though usually gentle, it takes on an intimidating look when protecting its family.

machamp.description: In close combat, its four arms afford it offensive and defensive supremacy. In but a blink, this valiant Pokémon can overwhelm its foes with more than 1,000 blows from its fists.
