machoke.description: A sturdy creature boasting a robust physique and boundless stamina. Loves training above all else and voluntarily assists with tasks such as construction and clearing land.

machop.description: Though as small as a child, it has strength enough to easily throw a well-built adult. Striving to become ever stronger, Machop trains by carrying a Graveler on its shoulders.

magby.description: This Pokémon lives in volcanic areas. With each breath, sparks spurt from its mouth and nose. When Magby is in good health, its flames gain a yellow tint.

magcargo.description: Magcargo’s body temperature is approximately 18,000 degrees Fahrenheit. Water is vaporized on contact. If this Pokémon is caught in the rain, the raindrops instantly turn into steam, cloaking the area in a thick fog.

magearna.description: Built roughly 500 years ago by a scientist, the part called the Soul-Heart is the actual life-form.

magikarp.description: A feeble, pitiful imbecile of a Pokémon that is nonetheless very hardy. Unperturbed by turbid water, it can be found living in all sorts of places.

magmar.description: Legend has it that this Pokémon was born from the crater of a volcano. When wounded, it bathes in lava to heal its body, much as one would soak in a hot spring.

magmortar.description: Use of a strange item caused this Pokémon to evolve. Fireballs launched from the ends of its tubelike arms are hot enough to melt an iron pot in an instant.

magnemite.description: A bizarre Pokémon with but a single eye embedded in an iron sphere. I suspect this creature levitates due to the magnetism it emits from its arms, which resemble horseshoe-shaped magnets.

magneton.description: Three Magnemite gathered to evolve into this Pokémon. The source of much vexation on my part, as its powerful magnetism destroys my research equipment.

magnezone.description: I theorize that a special magnetic field influenced this Pokémon, changing its molecular structure and causing it to evolve. It emits strange radio waves toward space from its antenna.

makuhita.description: There’s a rumor of a traditional recipe for stew that Trainers can use to raise strong Makuhita.

malamar.description: It’s said that Malamar’s hypnotic powers played a role in certain history-changing events.

mamoswine.description: This species reached its zenith during the period known as the ice age. I suspect that Hisui's frigid climate is in harmony with Mamoswine's constitution, thus awakening hidden potential.

manaphy.description: Rumored to migrate across the oceans and visit Hisui's coastal waters only rarely. Although Manaphy resembles Phione, it is also quite different. The relation between the two is unclear.

mandibuzz.description: They adorn themselves with bones. There seem to be fashion trends among them, as different bones come into and fall out of popularity.

manectric.description: It rarely appears before people. It is said to nest where lightning has fallen.

mankey.description: An agile Pokémon that lives in trees. It angers easily and will not hesitate to attack anything.

mantine.description: This calm and gentle Pokémon swims gracefully through the sea. After building speed, it can leap out of the water. It is often misidentified as a bird Pokémon due to this behavior.

mantyke.description: Though ball-like in shape, this Pokémon is a proficient swimmer. I have discovered that if a Mantyke spends much time with schools of Remoraid, it will eventually achieve evolution.

maractus.description: Once each year, this Pokémon scatters its seeds. They’re jam-packed with nutrients, making them a precious food source out in the desert.

mareanie.description: Unlike their Alolan counterparts, the Mareanie of the Galar region have not yet figured out that the branches of Corsola are delicious.

mareep.description: Rubbing its fleece generates electricity. You’ll want to pet it because it’s cute, but if you use your bare hand, you’ll get a painful shock.

marill.description: Even after Marill swims in a cold sea, its water- repellent fur dries almost as soon as Marill leaves the water. That’s why this Pokémon is never cold.

marowak.description: When this Pokémon evolved, the skull of its mother fused to it. Marowak’s temperament also turned vicious at the same time.

marshadow.description: This Pokémon can conceal itself in any shadow, so it went undiscovered for a long time.

marshtomp.description: Marshtomp is much faster at traveling through mud than it is at swimming. This Pokémon’s hindquarters exhibit obvious development, giving it the ability to walk on just its hind legs.

maschiff.description: Its well-developed jaw and fangs are strong enough to crunch through boulders, and its thick fat makes for an excellent defense.

masquerain.description: Its thin, winglike antennae are highly absorbent. It waits out rainy days in tree hollows.

maushold-family-of-four.description: The larger pair protects the little ones during battles. When facing strong opponents, the whole group will join the fight.

mawile.description: It chomps with its gaping mouth. Its huge jaws are actually steel horns that have been transformed.

medicham.description: Through the power of meditation, Medicham developed its sixth sense. It gained the ability to use psychokinetic powers. This Pokémon is known to meditate for a whole month without eating.

meditite.description: Meditite heightens its inner energy through meditation. It survives on just one berry a day. Minimal eating is another aspect of this Pokémon’s training.

meganium.description: The fragrance of Meganium’s flower soothes and calms emotions. In battle, this Pokémon gives off more of its becalming scent to blunt the foe’s fighting spirit.

melmetal.description: Centrifugal force is behind the punches of Melmetal’s heavy hex-nut arms. Melmetal is said to deliver the strongest punches of all Pokémon.

meloetta-aria.description: Its melodies are sung with a special vocalization method that can control the feelings of those who hear it.

meltan.description: They live as a group, but when the time comes, one strong Meltan will absorb all the others and evolve.

meowscarada.description: With skillful misdirection, it rigs foes with pollen-packed flower bombs. Meowscarada sets off the bombs before its foes realize what’s going on.

meowstic-male.description: The defensive instinct of the males is strong. It’s when they’re protecting themselves or their partners that they unleash their full power.

meowth.description: It washes its face regularly to keep the coin on its forehead spotless. It doesn’t get along with Galarian Meowth.

mesprit.description: Known as the Being of Emotion. In legend, this Pokémon was feared, as any who showed disrespect would have their emotions thrown into disarray.

metagross.description: Metagross is the result of the fusion of two Metang. This Pokémon defeats its opponents through use of its supercomputer-level brain.

metang.description: Using magnetic forces to stay aloft, this Pokémon flies at high speeds, weaving through harsh mountain terrain in pursuit of prey.

metapod.description: Even though it is encased in a sturdy shell, the body inside is tender. It can’t withstand a harsh attack.

mew.description: When viewed through a microscope, this Pokémon’s short, fine, delicate hair can be seen.

mewtwo.description: Its DNA is almost the same as Mew’s. However, its size and disposition are vastly different.

mienfoo.description: Though small, Mienfoo’s temperament is fierce. Any creature that approaches Mienfoo carelessly will be greeted with a flurry of graceful attacks.

mienshao.description: Delivered at blinding speeds, kicks from this Pokémon can shatter massive boulders into tiny pieces.

mightyena.description: Mightyena travel and act as a pack in the wild. The memory of its life in the wild compels the Pokémon to obey only those Trainers that it recognizes to possess superior skill.

milcery.description: They say that any patisserie visited by Milcery is guaranteed success and good fortune.

milotic.description: It’s said that a glimpse of a Milotic and its beauty will calm any hostile emotions you’re feeling.

miltank.description: This Pokémon needs to be milked every day, or else it will fall ill. The flavor of Miltank milk changes with the seasons.

mime-jr.description: Known to turn up in bustling marketplaces now and again. It mimics people much as a child would, then watches how they react, eyes sparkling.

mimikyu-disguised.description: There was a scientist who peeked under Mimikyu’s old rag in the name of research. The scientist died of a mysterious disease.

minccino.description: They pet each other with their tails as a form of greeting. Of the two, the one whose tail is fluffier is a bit more boastful.

minior-red-meteor.description: Although its outer shell is uncommonly durable, the shock of falling to the ground smashes the shell to smithereens.

minun.description: Minun loves to cheer on its partner in battle. It gives off sparks from its body while it is doing so. If its partner is in trouble, this Pokémon gives off increasing amounts of sparks.

miraidon.description: This seems to be the Iron Serpent mentioned in an old book. The Iron Serpent is said to have turned the land to ash with its lightning.

misdreavus.description: It conceals itself in darkness, sending chills up travelers' spines with its childlike weeping. As it observes the frightened travelers with glee, the red orbs upon its chest let off an eerie light.

mismagius.description: The incantations Mismagius chants can ward against misfortune, so a custom exists of inviting it into one's home. Incur the Pokémon's displeasure, however, and disaster will surely ensue.

moltres.description: There are stories of this Pokémon using its radiant, flame-cloaked wings to light up paths for those lost in the mountains.

monferno.description: The deeper the blue on its face, the more powerful it will grow to become. It leaps about every which way and lands powerful blows against its opponents with the flame on its tail.

morelull.description: Morelull live in forests that stay dark even during the day. They scatter flickering spores that put enemies to sleep.

morgrem.description: With sly cunning, it tries to lure people into the woods. Some believe it to have the power to make crops grow.

morpeko-full-belly.description: It carries electrically roasted seeds with it as if they’re precious treasures. No matter how much it eats, it always gets hungry again in short order.

mothim.description: Scatters steel-colored scales as it flaps its wings. Despite being observed feeding primarily on the nectar of flowers, Mothim is not often seen around flower gardens.

mr-mime.description: The behavior of this clown-like Pokémon reminds one of pantomime. It creates invisible walls using a force emitted from its fingertips.

mr-rime.description: Its amusing movements make it very popular. It releases its psychic power from the pattern on its belly.

mudbray.description: It eats dirt to create mud and smears this mud all over its feet, giving them the grip needed to walk on rough terrain without slipping.

mudkip.description: In water, Mudkip breathes using the gills on its cheeks. If it is faced with a tight situation in battle, this Pokémon will unleash its amazing power—it can crush rocks bigger than itself.

mudsdale.description: Mudsdale has so much stamina that it could carry over 10 tons across the Galar region without rest or sleep.

muk.description: Smells so awful, it can cause fainting. Through degeneration of its nose, it lost its sense of smell.

munchlax.description: Its robust stomach allows it to nonchalantly devour even rotted matter. It pays frequent visits to villages, seeking out food scraps intended for compost.

munkidori.description: Munkidori keeps itself somewhere safe while it toys with its foes, using psychokinesis to induce intense dizziness.

munna.description: It eats dreams and releases mist. The mist is pink when it’s eating a good dream, and black when it’s eating a nightmare.

murkrow.description: Widely shunned as a bearer of ill fortune. Upon crossing paths with this creature, I've been told one must chant ”Workrum, Workrum—bad luck, don't come” as a protective incantation.

musharna.description: It drowses and dreams all the time. It’s best to leave it be if it’s just woken up, as it’s a terrible grump when freshly roused from sleep.

nacli.description: The ground scrapes its body as it travels, causing it to leave salt behind. Salt is constantly being created and replenished inside Nacli’s body.

naclstack.description: It compresses rock salt inside its body and shoots out hardened salt pellets with enough force to perforate an iron sheet.

naganadel.description: One kind of Ultra Beast, it fires a glowing, venomous liquid from its needles. This liquid is also immensely adhesive.

natu.description: Because its wings aren’t yet fully grown, it has to hop to get around. It is always staring at something.

necrozma.description: It needs light to survive, and it goes on a rampage seeking it out. Its laser beams will cut anything to pieces.

nickit.description: Cunning and cautious, this Pokémon survives by stealing food from others. It erases its tracks with swipes of its tail as it makes off with its plunder.

nidoking.description: Nidoking prides itself on its strength. It’s forceful and spirited in battle, making use of its thick tail and diamond-crushing horn.

nidoqueen.description: It pacifies offspring by placing them in the gaps between the spines on its back. The spines will never secrete poison while young are present.

nidoran-f.description: It uses its hard incisor teeth to crush and eat berries. The tip of a female Nidoran’s horn is a bit more rounded than the tip of a male’s horn.

nidoran-m.description: Small but brave, this Pokémon will hold its ground and even risk its life in battle to protect the female it’s friendly with.

nidorina.description: If the group is threatened, these Pokémon will band together to assault enemies with a chorus of ultrasonic waves.

nidorino.description: It’s nervous and quick to act aggressively. The potency of its poison increases along with the level of adrenaline present in its body.

nihilego.description: It appeared in this world from an Ultra Wormhole. Nihilego appears to be a parasite that lives by feeding on people and Pokémon.

nincada.description: It can sometimes live underground for more than 10 years. It absorbs nutrients from the roots of trees.

ninetales.description: The coat of gleaming golden fur is quite magnificent. This species is said to store sacred power in its nine long tails and to live for a millennium.

ninjask.description: This Pokémon is so quick, it is said to be able to avoid any attack. It loves to feed on tree sap.

noctowl.description: When it needs to think, it rotates its head 180 degrees to sharpen its intellectual power.

noibat.description: No wavelength of sound is beyond Noibat’s ability to produce. The ultrasonic waves it generates can overcome much larger Pokémon.

noivern.description: Flying through the darkness, it weakens enemies with ultrasonic waves that could crush stone. Its fangs finish the fight.

nosepass.description: Once the people of Hisui discovered that its red nose always points north, they grew to rely on it greatly when traveling afar. The nose seems to work in a similar way to ancient compasses.

numel.description: Numel stores magma of almost 2,200 degrees Fahrenheit within its body. If it gets wet, the magma cools and hardens. In that event, the Pokémon’s body grows heavy and its movements become sluggish.

nuzleaf.description: They live in holes bored in large trees. The sound of Nuzleaf’s grass flute fills listeners with dread.

nymble.description: It’s highly skilled at a fighting style in which it uses its jumping capabilities to dodge incoming attacks while also dealing damage to opponents.

obstagoon.description: It evolved after experiencing numerous fights. While crossing its arms, it lets out a shout that would make any opponent flinch.

octillery.description: While Octillery still shoots water from its mouth, the drastic anatomical difference between it and Remoraid meant that for a long time, no one believed the former evolved from the latter.

oddish.description: During the day, it stays in the cold underground to avoid the sun. It grows by bathing in moonlight.

ogerpon.description: This mischief-loving Pokémon is full of curiosity. It battles by drawing out the type-based energy contained within its masks.

oinkologne-male.description: It entrances female Pokémon with the sweet, alluring scent that wafts from all over its body.

okidogi.description: Okidogi is a ruffian with a short temper. It can pulverize anything by swinging around the chain on its neck.

omanyte.description: This Pokémon is a member of an ancient, extinct species. Omanyte paddles through water with its 10 tentacles, looking like it’s just drifting along.

omastar.description: Omastar’s sharp fangs could crush rock, but the Pokémon can attack only the prey that come within reach of its tentacles.

onix.description: This chain of immense stones resembles a giant serpent. Tremors shake the earth above as it burrows deep beneath the ground, feeding on boulders as it goes.

oranguru.description: It knows the forest inside and out. If it comes across a wounded Pokémon, Oranguru will gather medicinal herbs to treat it.

orbeetle.description: It emits psychic energy to observe and study what’s around it—and what’s around it can include things over six miles away.

oricorio-baile.description: This Oricorio has drunk red nectar. If its Trainer gives the wrong order, this passionate Pokémon becomes fiercely angry.

orthworm.description: This Pokémon lives in arid deserts. It maintains its metal body by consuming iron from the soil.

oshawott.description: This Pokémon from the Unova region uses the shell on its belly as a weapon to cut down its foes. Thus, I've conferred upon this shell the name ”scalchop”.

overqwil.description: Its lancelike spikes and savage temperament have earned it the nickname ”sea fiend.” It slurps up poison to nourish itself.

pachirisu.description: A species related to the Pikachu line. Though Pachirisu is a calm Pokémon, it still presents a danger should one touch its electrified tail or cheeks.

palafin-zero.description: Its physical capabilities are no different than a Finizen’s, but when its allies are in danger, it transforms and powers itself up.

palkia.description: This Pokémon is feared as a deity in Hisuian legend. The birth of Palkia was what caused the walls of our world to disappear, creating a sky that spans for infinity.

palossand.description: This Pokémon lives on beaches, but it hates water. Palossand can’t maintain its castle-like shape if it gets drenched by a heavy rain.

palpitoad.description: On occasion, their cries are sublimely pleasing to the ear. Palpitoad with larger lumps on their bodies can sing with a wider range of sounds.

pancham.description: Wanting to make sure it’s taken seriously, Pancham’s always giving others a glare. But if it’s not focusing, it ends up smiling.

pangoro.description: Using its leaf, Pangoro can predict the moves of its opponents. It strikes with punches that can turn a dump truck into scrap with just one hit.

panpour.description: The water stored inside the tuft on its head is full of nutrients. Plants that receive its water grow large.

pansage.description: It’s good at finding berries and gathers them from all over. It’s kind enough to share them with friends.

pansear.description: This Pokémon lives in caves in volcanoes. The fire within the tuft on its head can reach 600 degrees Fahrenheit.

paras.description: Sometimes seen at the foot of trees in humid forests. The mushrooms on its back—called tochukaso—are not present on infant specimens and instead emerge as Paras matures.

parasect.description: Mushroom-lacking specimens of this Pokémon lie unmoving in the forest, lending credence to the hypothesis that the large mushroom is in control of Parasect's actions.

passimian.description: Passimian live in groups of about 20, with each member performing an assigned role. Through cooperation, the group survives.

patrat.description: Extremely cautious, one of them will always be on the lookout, but it won’t notice a foe coming from behind.

pawmi.description: The pads of its paws are electricity-discharging organs. Pawmi fires electricity from its forepaws while standing unsteadily on its hind legs.

pawmo.description: Pawmo uses a unique fighting technique in which it uses its forepaws to strike foes and zap them with electricity from its paw pads simultaneously.

pawmot.description: Pawmot’s fluffy fur acts as a battery. It can store the same amount of electricity as an electric car.

pawniard.description: A pack of these Pokémon forms to serve a Bisharp boss. Each Pawniard trains diligently, dreaming of one day taking the lead.

pecharunt.description: Its peach-shaped shell serves as storage for a potent poison. It makes poisonous mochi and serves them to people and Pokémon.

pelipper.description: Skimming the water’s surface, it dips its large bill in the sea, scoops up food and water, and carries it.

perrserker.description: After many battles, it evolved dangerous claws that come together to form daggers when extended.

persian.description: Its elegant and refined behavior clashes with that of the barbaric Perrserker. The relationship between the two is one of mutual disdain.

petilil.description: The leaves on its head are highly valued for medicinal purposes. Dry the leaves in the sun, boil them, and then drink the bitter decoction for remarkably effective relief from fatigue.

phanpy.description: Phanpy uses its long nose to shower itself. When others gather around, they thoroughly douse each other with water. These Pokémon can be seen drying their soaking-wet bodies at the edge of water.

phantump.description: With a voice like a human child’s, it cries out to lure adults deep into the forest, getting them lost among the trees.

pheromosa.description: Although it’s alien to this world and a danger here, it’s apparently a common organism in the world where it normally lives.

phione.description: Can be seen floating offshore during seasons when the seas are warm. Its azure body blends in with the ocean waters—logic suggests this is a defense mechanism against natural predators.

pichu.description: Pichu stores electricity in the sacs on its cheeks but discharges it inadvertently when agitated or excited. Being yet immature, the Pokémon's handling of electricity is rather inept.

pidgeot.description: This Pokémon flies at Mach 2 speed, seeking prey. Its large talons are feared as wicked weapons.

pidgeotto.description: This Pokémon is full of vitality. It constantly flies around its large territory in search of prey.

pidgey.description: Very docile. If attacked, it will often kick up sand to protect itself rather than fight back.

pidove.description: It’s forgetful and not very bright, but many Trainers love it anyway for its friendliness and sincerity.

pignite.description: When its internal fire flares up, its movements grow sharper and faster. When in trouble, it emits smoke.

pikachu.description: Possesses cheek sacs in which it stores electricity. This clever forest-dweller roasts tough berries with an electric shock before consuming them.

pikipek.description: It may look spindly, but its neck muscles are heavy-duty. It can peck at a tree 16 times per second!

piloswine.description: The long fur of this Pokémon covers its eyes, ears, and even limbs, allowing Piloswine to resist harshly frigid conditions. The Pokémon's white tusks can be used to defeat its enemies.

pincurchin.description: It stores electricity in each spine. Even if one gets broken off, it still continues to emit electricity for at least three hours.

pineco.description: It sticks tree bark to itself with its saliva, making itself thicker and larger. Elderly Pineco are ridiculously huge.

pinsir.description: This Pokémon clamps its pincers down on its prey and then either splits the prey in half or flings it away.

piplup.description: Prefers cold climes and appears along coasts. It's an adorable little thing—as cute as any child—but it's also prideful, unwilling to accept handouts from people.

plusle.description: When Plusle is cheering on its partner, it flashes with electric sparks from all over its body. If its partner loses, this Pokémon cries loudly.

poipole.description: An Ultra Beast that lives in a different world, it cackles wildly as it sprays its opponents with poison from the needles on its head.

politoed.description: The cry of a male is louder than that of a female. Male Politoed with deep, menacing voices find more popularity with the opposite gender.

poliwag.description: In rivers with fast-flowing water, this Pokémon will cling to a rock by using its thick lips, which act like a suction cup.

poliwhirl.description: This Pokémon’s sweat is a slimy mucus. When captured, Poliwhirl can slither from its enemies’ grasp and escape.

poliwrath.description: Poliwrath is skilled at both swimming and martial arts. It uses its well-trained arms to dish out powerful punches.

poltchageist.description: Poltchageist looks like a regional form of Sinistea, but it was recently discovered that the two Pokémon are entirely unrelated.

polteageist.description: Leaving leftover black tea unattended is asking for this Pokémon to come along and pour itself into it, turning the tea into a new Polteageist.

ponyta.description: These Pokémon live in herds out in the grassland. Newborn foals lack their fiery manes, which will develop about an hour after birth.

poochyena.description: Poochyena is an omnivore—it will eat anything. A distinguishing feature is how large its fangs are compared to its body. This Pokémon tries to intimidate its foes by making the hair on its tail bristle out.

popplio.description: If Popplio want to create big, powerful balloons, they must be persistent. It takes daily practice for these Pokémon to develop their skills.

porygon.description: It has no discernible heartbeat and does not seem to draw breath, and yet it appears to function without issue. I cannot even begin to explain this utterly bizarre anomaly.

porygon-z.description: A curious item induced this evolution. The Pokémon's offensive capabilities have greatly increased, but the strangeness of its behavior has magnified in equal measure. This worries me.

porygon2.description: A bizarre item caused this Pokémon to evolve. While it now exhibits many new gestures and expressions, its biology remains inscrutable.

primarina.description: For Primarina, every battle’s a stage. Its singing and the dancing of its balloons will mesmerize the audience.

primeape.description: It stops being angry only when nobody else is around. To view this moment is very difficult.

prinplup.description: It swims gracefully through the frigid sea and sings with a voice like the roaring tide. It has powerful, sturdy wings and dignity to match.

probopass.description: It is able to emit powerful magnetism, allowing it control over the iron sand that forms its luscious mustache. Using this iron sand, Probopass forms hard stones with which it smites its prey.

psyduck.description: Suffers perpetual headaches. If the agony grows too great, Psyduck's latent power erupts, contrary to Psyduck's intent. Ergo, I am exploring ways to ease the pain.

pumpkaboo-average.description: The light that streams out from the holes in the pumpkin can hypnotize and control the people and Pokémon that see it.

pupitar.description: It will not stay still, even while it’s a pupa. It already has arms and legs under its solid shell.

purrloin.description: Opponents that get drawn in by its adorable behavior come away with stinging scratches from its claws and stinging pride from its laughter.

purugly.description: Though impudent and difficult to tame, Purugly enjoys great popularity due to its fur, the beauty of which surpasses even velveteen.

pyroar-male.description: The temperature of its breath is over 10,000 degrees Fahrenheit, but Pyroar doesn’t use it on its prey. This Pokémon prefers to eat raw meat.

pyukumuku.description: It’s covered in a slime that keeps its skin moist, allowing it to stay on land for days without drying up.

quagsire.description: Its body is always slimy. It often bangs its head on the river bottom as it swims but seems not to care.

quaquaval.description: Dancing in ways that evoke far-away places, this Pokémon mesmerizes all that see it. Flourishes of its decorative water feathers slice into its foes.

quaxly.description: Its strong legs let it easily swim around in even fast-flowing rivers. It likes to keep things tidy and is prone to overthinking things.

quaxwell.description: The hardworking Quaxwell observes people and Pokémon from various regions and incorporates their movements into its own dance routines.

quilava.description: This creature's fur is most mysterious—it is wholly impervious to the burning touch of flame. Should Quilava turn its back to you, take heed! Such a posture indicates a forthcoming attack.

quilladin.description: They strengthen their lower bodies by running into one another. They are very kind and won’t start fights.

qwilfish.description: Fishers detest this troublesome Pokémon because it sprays poison from its spines, getting it everywhere. A different form of Qwilfish lives in other regions.

raboot.description: It kicks berries right off the branches of trees and then juggles them with its feet, practicing its footwork.

rabsca.description: An infant sleeps inside the ball. Rabsca rolls the ball soothingly with its legs to ensure the infant sleeps comfortably.

raging-bolt.description: It bears resemblance to a Pokémon that became a hot topic for a short while after a paranormal magazine touted it as Raikou's ancestor.

raichu.description: It can discharge bursts of electricity exceeding 100,000 volts— a single strike with that amount of power would incapacitate one of the Copperajah of my homeland.

raikou.description: Raikou embodies the speed of lightning. The roars of this Pokémon send shock waves shuddering through the air and shake the ground as if lightning bolts had come crashing down.

ralts.description: Tends to prefer people with a chipper disposition to those who are gloomy, but it has shown no discrimination with regard to age or gender. Needs more research.

rampardos.description: Very little is known about its biology. Can knock down massive trees by smashing its beautiful, pearl-like crown against them.

rapidash.description: Fiery mane aglow, Rapidash darts like an arrow across the land. This prodigiously swift creature can traverse the vast region of Hisui in a day and a half.

raticate.description: Its hind feet are webbed. They act as flippers, so it can swim in rivers and hunt for prey.

rattata.description: Will chew on anything with its fangs. If you see one, you can be certain that 40 more live in the area.

rayquaza.description: It flies forever through the ozone layer, consuming meteoroids for sustenance. The many meteoroids in its body provide the energy it needs to Mega Evolve.

regice.description: This Pokémon’s body is made of solid ice. It’s said that Regice was born beneath thick ice in the ice age.

regidrago.description: Its body is composed of crystallized dragon energy. Regidrago is said to have the powers of every dragon Pokémon.

regieleki.description: Its entire body is made up of a single organ that generates electrical energy. Regieleki is capable of creating all Galar’s electricity.

regigigas.description: According to legend, Regigigas pulled landmasses together and bound them with rope to create the continent of Hisui. Though I have my doubts, the story could well contain a shred of truth.

regirock.description: Cutting-edge technology was used to study the internals of this Pokémon’s rock body, but nothing was found—not even a brain or a heart.

registeel.description: It’s rumored that this Pokémon was born deep underground in the planet’s mantle and that it emerged onto the surface 10,000 years ago.

relicanth.description: This Pokémon was discovered during deep-sea exploration. Its appearance hasn’t changed in 100,000,000 years, so it’s called a living fossil.

rellor.description: It rolls its mud ball around while the energy it needs for evolution matures. Eventually the time comes for it to evolve.

remoraid.description: Spits water from its mouth with incredible accuracy. It captures Burmy by shooting them down off the branches from which they dangle.

reshiram.description: According to myth, if people ignore truth and let themselves become consumed by greed, Reshiram will arrive to burn their kingdoms down.

reuniclus.description: It’s said that drinking the liquid surrounding Reuniclus grants wisdom. Problem is, the liquid is highly toxic to anything besides Reuniclus itself.

revavroom.description: Revavroom viciously threatens others with the sound of its exhaust. It sticks its tongue out from its cylindrical mouth and sprays toxic fluids.

rhydon.description: Rapidly rotates its horn to bore through bedrock. It swaggers around volcanic regions, protected from the lava's heat by its tough, armorlike hide.

rhyhorn.description: Ludicrously strong—when it butts heads with a mountain, it is the mountain that shatters. But its short legs struggle with turns, and it is incapable of stopping unless it collides with something.

rhyperior.description: This Pokémon evolved through use of a curious item. Its rocklike hide is composed of a mysterious substance and can withstand a blow from a masterwork sword with nary a scratch.

ribombee.description: Ribombee absolutely hate getting wet or rained on. In the cloudy Galar region, they are very seldom seen.

rillaboom.description: The one with the best drumming techniques becomes the boss of the troop. It has a gentle disposition and values harmony among its group.

riolu.description: Though infantile in appearance, it has the mysterious ability to read the minds of humans. The pure of heart are met with Riolu's approval, while those of ill nature earn only its loathing.

roaring-moon.description: According to an article in a dubious magazine, this Pokémon has some connection to a phenomenon that occurs in a certain region.

rockruff.description: This Pokémon intimidates opponents by striking the ground with the rocks on its neck. The moment an opponent flinches, Rockruff attacks.

roggenrola.description: When it detects a noise, it starts to move. The energy core inside it makes this Pokémon slightly warm to the touch.

rolycoly.description: It can race around like a unicycle, even on rough, rocky terrain. Burning coal sustains it.

rookidee.description: Jumping nimbly about, this small-bodied Pokémon takes advantage of even the slightest opportunity to disorient larger opponents.

roselia.description: Though beautiful, it has highly poisonous thorns. There is an old tradition in my homeland wherein one would send these thorns to an opponent to challenge them to a duel.

roserade.description: Hidden within the bouquet on each hand are thorned whips loaded with virulent poison. Roserade moves gracefully as it corners its prey and mercilessly lashes them with its whips.

rotom.description: This bizarre Pokémon appears to be a will-o'-the-wisp powered by electricity. Be wary, as Rotom is both smart and mischievous.

rowlet.description: Flies noiselessly on delicate wings. It has mastered the art of deftly launching dagger-sharp feathers from those same wings.

rufflet.description: Its chick-like looks belie its hotheadedness. It challenges its parents at every opportunity, desperate to prove its strength.

runerigus.description: Never touch its shadowlike body, or you’ll be shown the horrific memories behind the picture carved into it.

sableye.description: It feeds on gemstone crystals. In darkness, its eyes sparkle with the glitter of jewels.

salamence.description: While basking in the joy of flight generally keeps this Pokémon in high spirits, Salamence turns into an uncontrollable menace if something angers it.

salandit.description: This sneaky Pokémon will slink behind its prey and immobilize it with poisonous gas before the prey even realizes Salandit is there.

salazzle.description: The winner of competitions between Salazzle is decided by which one has the most male Salandit with it.

samurott.description: Hard of heart and deft of blade, this rare form of Samurott is a product of the Pokémon's evolution in the region of Hisui. Its turbulent blows crash into foes like ceaseless pounding waves.

sandaconda.description: Its unique style of coiling allows it to blast sand out of its sand sac more efficiently.

sandile.description: Sandile is small, but its legs and lower body are powerful. Pushing sand aside as it goes, Sandile moves through the desert as if it’s swimming.

sandshrew.description: It burrows into the ground to create its nest. If hard stones impede its tunneling, it uses its sharp claws to shatter them and then carries on digging.

sandslash.description: It climbs trees by hooking on with its sharp claws. Sandslash shares the berries it gathers, dropping them down to Sandshrew waiting below the tree.

sandy-shocks.description: It slightly resembles a Magneton that lived for 10,000 years and was featured in an article in a paranormal magazine.

sandygast.description: Sandygast mainly inhabits beaches. It takes control of anyone who puts their hand into its mouth, forcing them to make its body bigger.

sawk.description: The karate chops of a Sawk that’s trained itself to the limit can cleave the ocean itself.

sawsbuck.description: They migrate according to the seasons, so some people call Sawsbuck the harbingers of spring.

scatterbug.description: The powder that covers its body regulates its temperature, so it can live in any region or climate.

sceptile.description: Sceptile has seeds growing on its back. They are said to be bursting with nutrients that revitalize trees. This Pokémon raises the trees in a forest with loving care.

scizor.description: Evolved by way of a curious item. The shell covering its body has been shown to be stronger than forged steel.

scolipede.description: Scolipede engage in fierce territorial battles with Centiskorch. At the end of one of these battles, the victor makes a meal of the loser.

scorbunny.description: It has special pads on the backs of its feet, and one on its nose. Once it’s raring to fight, these pads radiate tremendous heat.

scovillain.description: The green head has turned vicious due to the spicy chemicals stimulating its brain. Once it goes on a rampage, there is no stopping it.

scrafty.description: While mostly known for having the temperament of an aggressive ruffian, this Pokémon takes very good care of its family, friends, and territory.

scraggy.description: It protects itself with its durable skin. It’s thought that this Pokémon will evolve once its skin has completely stretched out.

scream-tail.description: It resembles a mysterious Pokémon described in a paranormal magazine as a Jigglypuff from one billion years ago.

scyther.description: The large, wickedly sharp scythes on its forearms are truly fearsome weapons. Prey's attempts to flee are unfailingly thwarted by this Pokémon's nimble motions.

seadra.description: Seadra’s mouth is slender, but its suction power is strong. In an instant, Seadra can suck in food that’s larger than the opening of its mouth.

seaking.description: Using its horn, it bores holes in riverbed boulders, making nests to prevent its eggs from washing away.

sealeo.description: Its white whiskers are very sensitive. Sealeo will balance Spheal on the tip of its nose, checking its scent and its feel to be sure the Spheal is healthy.

seedot.description: It attaches itself to a tree branch using the top of its head. Strong winds can sometimes make it fall.

seel.description: Loves freezing-cold conditions. Relishes swimming in a frigid climate of around 14 degrees Fahrenheit.

seismitoad.description: This Pokémon is popular among the elderly, who say the vibrations of its lumps are great for massages.

sentret.description: When Sentret sleeps, it does so while another stands guard. The sentry wakes the others at the first sign of danger. When this Pokémon becomes separated from its pack, it becomes incapable of sleep due to fear.

serperior.description: It can stop its opponents’ movements with just a glare. It takes in solar energy and boosts it internally.

servine.description: When it gets dirty, its leaves can’t be used in photosynthesis, so it always keeps itself clean.

seviper.description: Seviper’s swordlike tail serves two purposes—it slashes foes and douses them with secreted poison. This Pokémon will not give up its long-running blood feud with Zangoose.

sewaddle.description: Since this Pokémon makes its own clothes out of leaves, it is a popular mascot for fashion designers.

sharpedo.description: This Pokémon is known as the Bully of the Sea. Any ship entering the waters Sharpedo calls home will be attacked—no exceptions.

shaymin-land.description: When the turning of seasons brings the cruel winter to its end and the joyous people give thanks to the heavens, Shaymin appears and covers the withered land with flowers.

shedinja.description: A strange Pokémon—it flies without moving its wings, has a hollow shell for a body, and does not breathe.

shelgon.description: Shelgon ignores its hunger entirely, never eating any food. Apparently, Shelgon will evolve once all its energy stores are used up.

shellder.description: Its hard shell repels any kind of attack. It is vulnerable only when its shell is open.

shellos.description: Found in abundance on seashores bordering warm waters. Shellos are unexpectedly friendly and will crawl toward any person they see. Take care not to get coated in mucus!

shelmet.description: It has a strange physiology that responds to electricity. When together with Karrablast, Shelmet evolves for some reason.

shieldon.description: Much remains unknown about this Pokémon, as few have ever seen it. However, we know that it is calm and dislikes conflict, and it enjoys polishing its face against trees and rocks.

shiftry.description: It lives quietly in the deep forest. It is said to create chilly winter winds with the fans it holds.

shiinotic.description: If you see a light deep in a forest at night, don’t go near. Shiinotic will make you fall fast asleep.

shinx.description: Shakes its body to generate electricity. Its stature belies its aggression—one must be patient to tame this Pokémon.

shroodle.description: To keep enemies away from its territory, it paints markings around its nest using a poisonous liquid that has an acrid odor.

shroomish.description: If Shroomish senses danger, it shakes its body and scatters spores from the top of its head. This Pokémon’s spores are so toxic, they make trees and weeds wilt.

shuckle.description: The berries stored in its vaselike shell eventually become a thick, pulpy juice.

shuppet.description: There’s a proverb that says, “Shun the house where Shuppet gather in the growing dusk.”

sigilyph.description: A discovery was made in the desert where Sigilyph fly. The ruins of what may have been an ancient city were found beneath the sands.

silcoon.description: Wraps itself in thin strings of silk while it stores energy for evolution. It can't extend its limbs and its movement is slow, but its eyes keep a sharp lookout—Silcoon is always on guard.

silicobra.description: It spews sand from its nostrils. While the enemy is blinded, it burrows into the ground to hide.

silvally.description: The final factor needed to release this Pokémon’s true power was a strong bond with a Trainer it trusts.

simipour.description: It prefers places with clean water. When its tuft runs low, it replenishes it by siphoning up water with its tail.

simisage.description: Ill tempered, it fights by swinging its barbed tail around wildly. The leaf growing on its head is very bitter.

simisear.description: When it gets excited, embers rise from its head and tail and it gets hot. For some reason, it loves sweets.

sinistcha.description: It prefers cool, dark places, such as the back of a shelf or the space beneath a home's floorboards. It wanders in search of prey after sunset.

sinistea.description: The teacup in which this Pokémon makes its home is a famous piece of antique tableware. Many forgeries are in circulation.

sirfetchd.description: After deflecting attacks with its hard leaf shield, it strikes back with its sharp leek stalk. The leek stalk is both weapon and food.

sizzlipede.description: It wraps prey up with its heated body, cooking them in its coils. Once they’re well-done, it will voraciously nibble them down to the last morsel.

skarmory.description: People fashion swords from Skarmory’s shed feathers, so this Pokémon is a popular element in heraldic designs.

skeledirge.description: Skeledirge’s gentle singing soothes the souls of all that hear it. It burns its enemies to a crisp with flames of over 5,400 degrees Fahrenheit.

skiddo.description: If it has sunshine and water, it doesn’t need to eat, because it can generate energy from the leaves on its back.

skiploom.description: Skiploom’s flower blossoms when the temperature rises above 64 degrees Fahrenheit. How much the flower opens depends on the temperature. For that reason, this Pokémon is sometimes used as a thermometer.

skitty.description: Skitty is known to chase around playfully after its own tail. In the wild, this Pokémon lives in holes in the trees of forests. It is very popular as a pet because of its adorable looks.

skorupi.description: Its claws are not only razor-sharp but poisonous, making Skorupi a highly dangerous Pokémon. It seems to be weakened by cold temperatures, however.

skrelp.description: Skrelp looks like a piece of rotten seaweed, so it can blend in with seaweed drifting on the ocean and avoid being detected by enemies.

skuntank.description: Sprays a poisonous fluid to take down prey. Sometimes, unable to stomach the stench of its own fluid, it leaves the bested prey uneaten.

skwovet.description: It eats berries nonstop—a habit that has made it more resilient than it looks. It’ll show up on farms, searching for yet more berries.

slaking.description: Wherever Slaking live, rings of over a yard in diameter appear in grassy fields. They are made by the Pokémon as it eats all the grass within reach while lying prone on the ground.

slakoth.description: Slakoth’s heart beats just once a minute. Whatever happens, it is content to loaf around motionless. It is rare to see this Pokémon in motion.

sliggoo.description: A creature given to melancholy. I suspect its metallic shell developed as a result of the mucus on its skin reacting with the iron in Hisui's water.

slither-wing.description: This Pokémon somewhat resembles an ancient form of Volcarona that was introduced in a dubious magazine.

slowbro.description: Being bitten by a Shellder shocked this Pokémon into standing on two legs. If the Shellder lets go, it seems Slowbro will turn back into a Slowpoke.

slowking.description: Slowking can solve any problem presented to it, but no one can understand a thing Slowking says.

slowpoke.description: When this Pokémon’s tail is soaked in water, sweetness seeps from it. Slowpoke uses this trait to lure in and fish up other Pokémon.

slugma.description: Slugma does not have any blood in its body. Instead, intensely hot magma circulates throughout this Pokémon’s body, carrying essential nutrients and oxygen to its organs.

slurpuff.description: Slurpuff’s fur contains a lot of air, making it soft to the touch and lighter than it looks.

smeargle.description: It draws symbols with the fluid that oozes from the tip of its tail. Depending on the symbol, Smeargle fanatics will pay big money for them.

smoliv.description: This Pokémon converts nutrients into oil, which it stores in the fruit on its head. It can easily go a whole week without eating or drinking.

smoochum.description: This is a very curious Pokémon. Smoochum decides what it likes and dislikes by touching things with its lips.

sneasel.description: Its sturdy, curved claws are ideal for traversing precipitous cliffs. From the tips of these claws drips a venom that infiltrates the nerves of any prey caught in Sneasel's grasp.

sneasler.description: Because of Sneasler's virulent poison and daunting physical prowess, no other species could hope to best it on the frozen highlands. Preferring solitude, this species does not form packs.

snivy.description: They photosynthesize by bathing their tails in sunlight. When they are not feeling well, their tails droop.

snom.description: It eats snow that piles up on the ground. The more snow it eats, the bigger and more impressive the spikes on its back grow.

snorlax.description: This glutton appears in villages without warning and devours the entirety of their rice granaries—such occurrences have long been counted among the gravest of disasters.

snorunt.description: Arrives alongside the first snow. It's thought that homes Snorunt visit will prosper for many generations. By tradition, one might offer a lump of ice made from pure water at one's front door.

snover.description: One is likely to encounter this Pokémon while out in the snow. There are stories of Snover appearing in human settlements but doing no harm—rather, they bond with the children.

snubbull.description: In contrast to its appearance, it’s quite timid. When playing with other puppy Pokémon, it sometimes gets bullied.

sobble.description: When it gets wet, its skin changes color, and this Pokémon becomes invisible as if it were camouflaged.

solgaleo.description: Solgaleo was once known as the Beast That Devours the Sun. Energy in the form of light radiates boundlessly from it.

solosis.description: Many say that the special liquid covering this Pokémon’s body would allow it to survive in the vacuum of space.

solrock.description: Solar energy is the source of its power, so it is strong during the daytime. When it spins, its body shines.

spearow.description: Inept at flying high. However, it can fly around very fast to protect its territory.

spectrier.description: As it dashes through the night, Spectrier absorbs the life-force of sleeping creatures. It craves silence and solitude.

spewpa.description: The beaks of bird Pokémon can’t begin to scratch its stalwart body. To defend itself, it spews powder.

spheal.description: During the season when drift ice approaches the shore, Spheal prefers living on the ice—where fewer predators lurk—rather than the land. Its fur retains heat superbly and resists harsh cold.

spidops.description: Spidops covers its territory in tough, sticky threads to set up traps for intruders.

spinarak.description: Although the poison from its fangs isn’t that strong, it’s potent enough to weaken prey that gets caught in its web.

spinda.description: Each Spinda’s spot pattern is different. With its stumbling movements, it evades opponents’ attacks brilliantly!

spiritomb.description: It lays curses by thinking wicked thoughts. Writings tell that this Pokémon was born out of the assembly of five score and eight malevolent spirits.

spoink.description: Spoink keeps a pearl on top of its head. The pearl functions to amplify this Pokémon’s psychokinetic powers. It is therefore on a constant search for a bigger pearl.

sprigatito.description: The sweet scent its body gives off mesmerizes those around it. The scent grows stronger when this Pokémon is in the sun.

spritzee.description: The scent its body gives off enraptures those who smell it. Noble ladies had no shortage of love for Spritzee.

squawkabilly-green-plumage.description: Green-feathered flocks hold the most sway. When they’re out searching for food in the mornings and evenings, it gets very noisy.

squirtle.description: When it feels threatened, it draws its limbs inside its shell and sprays water from its mouth.

stakataka.description: When stone walls started moving and attacking, the brute’s true identity was this mysterious life-form, which brings to mind an Ultra Beast.

stantler.description: Its strangely shaped antlers have the power to bewitch those who see them. Medicine made by grinding up the black orbs from fallen antlers is an effective treatment for insomnia.

staraptor.description: It has left the flock, having gained strength enough to survive on its own. The astounding force with which Staraptor flies through the air allows it to carry away large, burly targets.

staravia.description: They form remarkably large flocks and are constantly fighting amongst themselves. I suspect that those with magnificent plumes on their heads are the strong ones.

starly.description: They live in the fields and mountains, gathering in large flocks. Their cries are quite obnoxious. Though small, their wings are strong—a strike from them leaves pain that persists for a week.

starmie.description: Starmie swims by spinning its body at high speed. As this Pokémon cruises through the ocean, it absorbs tiny plankton.

staryu.description: Fish Pokémon nibble at it, but Staryu isn’t bothered. Its body regenerates quickly, even if part of it is completely torn off.

steelix.description: This Pokémon evolved through use of a strange item. Its body is coated with steel powder and notably hard—not even diamond can leave so much as a scratch.

steenee.description: Any Corvisquire that pecks at this Pokémon will be greeted with a smack from its sepals followed by a sharp kick.

stonjourner.description: Once a year, on a specific date and at a specific time, they gather out of nowhere and form up in a circle.

stoutland.description: Stoutland is immensely proud of its impressive moustache. It’s said that moustache length is what determines social standing among this species.

stufful.description: The way it protects itself by flailing its arms may be an adorable sight, but stay well away. This is flailing that can snap thick tree trunks.

stunfisk.description: For some reason, this Pokémon smiles slightly when it emits a strong electric current from the yellow markings on its body.

stunky.description: The poison that gushes from its aft end is accompanied by an utterly evil-smelling odor with such potency that one whiff can induce memory loss.

sudowoodo.description: Though it pretends to be a tree, it fails to fool even children. To the touch, its body feels more like rock than tree bark. Sudowoodo's extreme aversion to water merits special note.

suicune.description: Suicune embodies the compassion of a pure spring of water. It runs across the land with gracefulness. This Pokémon has the power to purify dirty water.

sunflora.description: Sunflora converts solar energy into nutrition. It moves around actively in the daytime when it is warm. It stops moving as soon as the sun goes down for the night.

sunkern.description: Sunkern tries to move as little as it possibly can. It does so because it tries to conserve all the nutrients it has stored in its body for its evolution. It will not eat a thing, subsisting only on morning dew.

surskit.description: It lives in ponds and marshes that feature lots of plant life. It often fights with Dewpider, whose habitat and diet are similar.

swablu.description: Since Swablu looks like a cumulus cloud, foes can have a hard time finding it. Apparently its wings turned white over many generations.

swadloon.description: It protects itself from the cold by wrapping up in leaves. It stays on the move, eating leaves in forests.

swalot.description: Swalot has no teeth, so what it eats, it swallows whole, no matter what. Its cavernous mouth yawns widely. An automobile tire could easily fit inside this Pokémon’s mouth.

swampert.description: Swampert predicts storms by sensing subtle differences in the sounds of waves and tidal winds with its fins. If a storm is approaching, it piles up boulders to protect itself.

swanna.description: Swanna start to dance at dusk. The one dancing in the middle is the leader of the flock.

swellow.description: Swellow is very conscientious about the upkeep of its glossy wings. Once two Swellow are gathered, they diligently take care of cleaning each other’s wings.

swinub.description: Swinub excels at sniffing out mushrooms buried beneath grass or snow. Since ancient times, the people of Hisui have often relied upon this skill.

swirlix.description: The sweet smell of cotton candy perfumes Swirlix’s fluffy fur. This Pokémon spits out sticky string to tangle up its enemies.

swoobat.description: The auspicious shape of this Pokémon’s nose apparently led some regions to consider Swoobat a symbol of good luck.

sylveon.description: It emits a soothing aura from its ribbon-shaped organs. It wraps these appendages around quarrelers to instantly restore calm to the situation.

tadbulb.description: It floats using the electricity stored in its body. When thunderclouds are around, Tadbulb will float higher off the ground.

taillow.description: Taillow is young—it has only just left its nest. As a result, it sometimes becomes lonesome and cries at night. This Pokémon feeds on Wurmple that live in forests.

talonflame.description: Talonflame dives toward prey at speeds of up to 310 mph and assaults them with powerful kicks, giving the prey no chance to escape.

tandemaus.description: The pair sticks together no matter what. They split any food they find exactly in half and then eat it together.

tangela.description: It is cloaked entirely in blue vines, preventing any glimpse of its true identity. The vines impart a refreshing sensation when chewed—they're useful as a spice.

tangrowth.description: Draped with long vines, it resembles a shrub in appearance. It swings bundles of vines as though they were arms, wrapping them around prey to ensnare them.

tapu-bulu.description: It makes ringing sounds with its tail to let others know where it is, avoiding unneeded conflicts. This guardian deity of Ula’ula controls plants.

tapu-fini.description: Although it’s called a guardian deity, terrible calamities sometimes befall those who recklessly approach Tapu Fini.

tapu-koko.description: The lightning-wielding guardian deity of Melemele, Tapu Koko is brimming with curiosity and appears before people from time to time.

tapu-lele.description: Although called a guardian deity, Tapu Lele is devoid of guilt about its cruel disposition and can be described as nature incarnate.

tarountula.description: The thread it secretes from its rear is as strong as wire. The secret behind the thread’s strength is the topic of ongoing research.

tatsugiri-curly.description: Tatsugiri is an extremely cunning Pokémon. It feigns weakness to lure in prey, then orders its partner to attack.

tauros.description: The Tauros of the Galar region are volatile in nature, and they won’t allow people to ride on their backs.

teddiursa.description: It licks its paws because of the sweet honey that has soaked into them. It is cunning, stealing into the nests of Combee and taking for itself the honey that the Combee have amassed.

tentacool.description: They fire beams from the glassy, magenta orbs that resemble eyes atop their heads, and they drift in shallow seas. During low tide, they can sometimes be found on beaches, desiccated.

tentacruel.description: It has 80 tentacles, each with a venomous tip. These tentacles are also extendible, lengthening when Tentacruel attempts to catch prey. Use caution.

tepig.description: It loves to eat roasted berries, but sometimes it gets too excited and burns them to a crisp.

terapagos.description: It’s thought that this Pokémon lived in ancient Paldea until it got caught in seismic shifts and went extinct.

terrakion.description: In Unovan legend, Terrakion battled against humans in an effort to protect other Pokémon.

thievul.description: With a lithe body and sharp claws, it goes around stealing food and eggs. Boltund is its natural enemy.

throh.description: They train in groups of five. Any member that can’t keep up will discard its belt and leave the group.

thundurus-incarnate.description: They say this wielder of electricity has waged war with its nemesis, Tornadus, since time immemorial. The lightning bolts it hurls pierce the very earth and enrich the soil.

thwackey.description: When it’s drumming out rapid beats in battle, it gets so caught up in the rhythm that it won’t even notice that it’s already knocked out its opponent.

timburr.description: Timburr that have started carrying logs that are about three times their size are nearly ready to evolve.

ting-lu.description: It slowly brings its exceedingly heavy head down upon the ground, splitting the earth open with huge fissures that run over 160 feet deep.

tinkatink.description: This Pokémon pounds iron scraps together to make a hammer. It will remake the hammer again and again until it’s satisfied with the result.

tinkaton.description: The hammer tops 220 pounds, yet it gets swung around easily by Tinkaton as it steals whatever it pleases and carries its plunder back home.

tinkatuff.description: These Pokémon make their homes in piles of scrap metal. They test the strength of each other’s hammers by smashing them together.

tirtouga.description: Tirtouga is considered to be the ancestor of many turtle Pokémon. It was restored to life from a fossil.

toedscool.description: Though it looks like Tentacool, Toedscool is a completely different species. Its legs may be thin, but it can run at a speed of 30 mph.

toedscruel.description: It coils its 10 tentacles around prey and sucks out their nutrients, causing the prey pain. The folds along the rim of its head are a popular delicacy.

togedemaru.description: When it’s in trouble, it curls up into a ball, makes its fur spikes stand on end, and then discharges electricity indiscriminately.

togekiss.description: Scant few have ever sighted this Pokémon. After studying what literature remains, I am certain Togekiss will reveal itself when peace reigns in the land.

togepi.description: This ovate creature is frequently mistaken for a moving egg when encountered out in the fields or in the mountains. Its guileless smile soothes the soul.

togetic.description: No records exist of Togetic being seen in the wilds. Rumors abound that it evolves under the loving care of a trusted human companion, upon whom the Pokémon then bestows great joy.

torchic.description: Torchic has a place inside its body where it keeps its flame. Give it a hug—it will be glowing with warmth. This Pokémon is covered all over by a fluffy coat of down.

torkoal.description: You find abandoned coal mines full of them. They dig tirelessly in search of coal.

tornadus-incarnate.description: This storm-stirring Pokémon is said to cause the seasons to turn by whipping up the air. I suspect its humanlike form to be a false one.

torracat.description: When facing a powerful enemy, Torracat’s fighting spirit gets pumped up, and its fire bell blazes hotter.

torterra.description: This remarkable, large-bodied Pokémon would serve beautifully as borrowed scenery for a garden, and its strength is peerless. Torterra roams the wilderness in search of clean water.

totodile.description: Despite the smallness of its body, Totodile’s jaws are very powerful. While the Pokémon may think it is just playfully nipping, its bite has enough power to cause serious injury.

toucannon.description: Known for forming harmonious couples, this Pokémon is brought to wedding ceremonies as a good luck charm.

toxapex.description: Within the poison sac in its body is a poison so toxic that Pokémon as large as Wailord will still be suffering three days after it first takes effect.

toxel.description: It manipulates the chemical makeup of its poison to produce electricity. The voltage is weak, but it can cause a tingling paralysis.

toxicroak.description: Its crimson claws contain a virulent toxin. This toxin can be made into a tonic by diluting it, mixing it with several types of wild grass, and boiling it down over two days.

toxtricity-amped.description: This short-tempered and aggressive Pokémon chugs stagnant water to absorb any toxins it might contain.

tranquill.description: These bright Pokémon have acute memories. Apparently delivery workers often choose them as their partners.

trapinch.description: It makes an inescapable conical pit and lies in wait at the bottom for prey to come tumbling down.

treecko.description: Treecko is cool, calm, and collected—it never panics under any situation. If a bigger foe were to glare at this Pokémon, it would glare right back without conceding an inch of ground.

trevenant.description: Small roots that extend from the tips of this Pokémon’s feet can tie into the trees of the forest and give Trevenant control over them.

tropius.description: Bunches of delicious fruit grow around its neck. In warm areas, many ranches raise Tropius.

trubbish.description: This Pokémon was born from a bag stuffed with trash. Galarian Weezing relish the fumes belched by Trubbish.

trumbeak.description: From its mouth, it fires the seeds of berries it has eaten. The scattered seeds give rise to new plants.

tsareena.description: A kick from the hardened tips of this Pokémon’s legs leaves a wound in the opponent’s body and soul that will never heal.

turtonator.description: Eating sulfur in its volcanic habitat is what causes explosive compounds to develop in its shell. Its droppings are also dangerously explosive.

turtwig.description: This Pokémon becomes more energetic the more sunlight there is. The part resembling a shell is similar to silt and is slightly damp and warm to the touch.

tympole.description: It uses sound waves to communicate with others of its kind. People and other Pokémon species can’t hear its cries of warning.

tynamo.description: One alone can emit only a trickle of electricity, so a group of them gathers to unleash a powerful electric shock.

type-null.description: It was modeled after a mighty Pokémon of myth. The mask placed upon it limits its power in order to keep it under control.

typhlosion.description: Said to purify lost, forsaken souls with its flames and guide them to the afterlife. I believe its form has been influenced by the energy of the sacred mountain towering at Hisui's center.

tyranitar.description: The quakes caused when it walks make even great mountains crumble and change the surrounding terrain.

tyrantrum.description: A single bite of Tyrantrum’s massive jaws will demolish a car. This Pokémon was the king of the ancient world.

tyrogue.description: Even though it is small, it can’t be ignored because it will slug any handy target without warning.

tyrunt.description: This Pokémon is selfish and likes to be pampered. It can also inflict grievous wounds on its Trainer just by playing around.

umbreon.description: It is most active in the wee hours of the night, when moonlight bathes the land. Its large eyes can pierce the darkness and perceive prey with absolute clarity.

unfezant.description: This Pokémon is intelligent and intensely proud. People will sit up and take notice if you become the Trainer of one.

unown.description: It is hard to believe these strangely shaped Pokémon are truly living creatures. I've pointed out that the species' many forms resemble writing from other lands; no one will take me seriously.

ursaluna.description: I believe it was Hisui's swampy terrain that gave Ursaluna its burly physique and newfound capacity to manipulate peat at will.

ursaring.description: When the cold season arrives in Hisui, this Pokémon will wander fields and mountains alike in search of its favorite berries. Ursaring's hunger during this time makes it a ferocious danger.

urshifu-single-strike.description: Inhabiting the mountains of a distant region, this Pokémon races across sheer cliffs, training its legs and refining its moves.

uxie.description: A Pokémon feared but also respected for stealing away the memories of evildoers. I have found records that suggest Uxie holds dominion over knowledge.

vanillish.description: It blasts enemies with cold air reaching −148 degrees Fahrenheit, freezing them solid. But it spares their lives afterward—it’s a kind Pokémon.

vanillite.description: Supposedly, this Pokémon was born from an icicle. It spews out freezing air at −58 degrees Fahrenheit to make itself more comfortable.

vanilluxe.description: People believe this Pokémon formed when two Vanillish stuck together. Its body temperature is roughly 21 degrees Fahrenheit.

vaporeon.description: Tests show that its cells closely resemble water molecules, which perhaps explains its ability to conceal its form while submerged. I believe the origins of mermaid folklore lie with this Pokémon.

varoom.description: The steel section is Varoom’s actual body. This Pokémon clings to rocks and converts the minerals within into energy to fuel its activities.

veluza.description: Veluza has excellent regenerative capabilities. It sheds spare flesh from its body to boost its agility, then charges at its prey.

venipede.description: Its fangs are highly venomous. If this Pokémon finds prey it thinks it can eat, it leaps for them without any thought of how things might turn out.

venomoth.description: The powdery scales on its wings are hard to remove from skin. They also contain poison that leaks out on contact.

venonat.description: Its large eyes act as radar. In a bright place, you can see that they are clusters of many tiny eyes.

venusaur.description: A bewitching aroma wafts from its flower. The fragrance becalms those engaged in a battle.

vespiquen.description: Commands its subjects to build its hive. It will dispatch any interlopers who dare sneak into its nest and use them as nourishment for itself.

vibrava.description: To help make its wings grow, it dissolves quantities of prey in its digestive juices and guzzles them down every day.

victini.description: When it shares the infinite energy it creates, that being’s entire body will be overflowing with power.

victreebel.description: Lures prey with the sweet aroma of honey. Swallowed whole, the prey is dissolved in a day, bones and all.

vigoroth.description: Vigoroth is simply incapable of remaining still. Even when it tries to sleep, the blood in its veins grows agitated, compelling this Pokémon to run wild throughout the jungle before it can settle down.

vikavolt.description: If it carries a Charjabug to use as a spare battery, a flying Vikavolt can rapidly fire high-powered beams of electricity.

vileplume.description: The larger its petals, the more toxic pollen it contains. Its big head is heavy and hard to hold up.

virizion.description: It darts around opponents with a flurry of quick movements, slicing them up with its horns.

vivillon.description: The patterns on this Pokémon’s wings depend on the climate and topography of its habitat. It scatters colorful scales.

volbeat.description: Volbeat’s tail glows like a lightbulb. With other Volbeat, it uses its tail to draw geometric shapes in the night sky. This Pokémon loves the sweet aroma given off by Illumise.

volcanion.description: It expels its internal steam from the arms on its back. It has enough power to blow away a mountain.

volcarona.description: This Pokémon emerges from a cocoon formed of raging flames. Ancient murals depict Volcarona as a deity of fire.

voltorb.description: An enigmatic Pokémon that happens to bear a resemblance to a Poké Ball. When excited, it discharges the electric current it has stored in its belly, then lets out a great, uproarious laugh.

vullaby.description: Vullaby grow quickly. Bones that have gotten too small for older Vullaby to wear often get passed down to younger ones in the nest.

vulpix.description: In its belly burns a fire, which Vulpix spits out in the form of fireballs. When young, this Pokémon has but one white tail. As the Pokémon matures, this single tail splits into six.

wailmer.description: When it sucks in a large volume of seawater, it becomes like a big, bouncy ball. It eats a ton of food daily.

wailord.description: Its immense size is the reason for its popularity. Wailord watching is a favorite sightseeing activity in various parts of the world.

walking-wake.description: It resembles an illustration published in a paranormal magazine, said to be a depiction of a super-ancient Suicune.

walrein.description: Its thick tusks are strong enough to shatter drift ice. They have been known to break, but they will grow back by the next year. The Hisui region is well known for these broken tusks.

wartortle.description: It cleverly controls its furry ears and tail to maintain its balance while swimming.

watchog.description: When they see an enemy, their tails stand high, and they spit the seeds of berries stored in their cheek pouches.

wattrel.description: These Pokémon make their nests on coastal cliffs. The nests have a strange, crackling texture, and they’re a popular delicacy.

weavile.description: This species corners prey as a pack, under the guidance of a leader. Weavile displays increased cunning, leading me to speculate that its evolution caused further brain development.

weedle.description: Beware of the sharp stinger on its head. It hides in grass and bushes where it eats leaves.

weepinbell.description: When hungry, it swallows anything that moves. Its hapless prey is dissolved by strong acids.

weezing.description: It can’t suck in air quite as well as a Galarian Weezing, but the toxins it creates are more potent than those of its counterpart.

whimsicott.description: As long as this Pokémon bathes in sunlight, its cotton keeps growing. If too much cotton fluff builds up, Whimsicott tears it off and scatters it.

whirlipede.description: Whirlipede protects itself with a sturdy shell and poisonous spikes while it stores up the energy it’ll need for evolution.

whiscash.description: Strikes its caudal fin against the swamp bed to shake the ground and startle its prey. It will then swallow the fleeing prey whole. People mistook this behavior as the cause of earthquakes.

whismur.description: When Whismur cries, the sound of its own voice startles it, making the Pokémon cry even louder. It cries until it’s exhausted, then it falls asleep.

wigglytuff.description: It’s proud of its fur, which is fine and delicate. In particular, the curl on its forehead has a texture that’s perfectly heavenly.

wiglett.description: Though it looks like Diglett, Wiglett is an entirely different species. The resemblance seems to be a coincidental result of environmental adaptation.

wimpod.description: Wimpod gather in swarms, constantly on the lookout for danger. They scatter the moment they detect an enemy’s presence.

wingull.description: It soars on updrafts without flapping its wings. It makes a nest on sheer cliffs at the sea’s edge.

wishiwashi-solo.description: When it senses danger, its eyes tear up. The sparkle of its tears signals other Wishiwashi to gather.

wo-chien.description: It drains the life-force from vegetation, causing nearby forests to instantly wither and fields to turn barren.

wobbuffet.description: To keep its pitch-black tail hidden, it lives quietly in the darkness. It is never first to attack.

woobat.description: It emits ultrasonic waves as it flutters about, searching for its prey—bug Pokémon.

wooloo.description: If its fleece grows too long, Wooloo won’t be able to move. Cloth made with the wool of this Pokémon is surprisingly strong.

wooper.description: When walking on land, it covers its body with a poisonous film that keeps its skin from dehydrating.

wormadam-plant.description: When Burmy evolved, its cloak became a part of this Pokémon’s body. The cloak is never shed.

wugtrio.description: A variety of fish Pokémon, Wugtrio was once considered to be a regional form of Dugtrio.

wurmple.description: Likes sap and is abundant in the wild. Why it evolves into various different forms is unknown. One cannot tell from a Wurmple's appearance which form it will take when it evolves.

wynaut.description: It tends to move in a pack with others. They cluster in a tight group to sleep in a cave.

wyrdeer.description: The black orbs shine with an uncanny light when the Pokémon is erecting invisible barriers. The fur shed from its beard retains heat well and is a highly useful material for winter clothing.

xatu.description: This odd Pokémon can see both the past and the future. It eyes the sun’s movement all day.

xerneas.description: When the horns on its head shine in seven colors, it is said to be sharing everlasting life.

xurkitree.description: They’ve been dubbed Ultra Beasts. Some of them stand unmoving, like trees, with their arms and legs stuck into the ground.

yamask.description: The spirit of a person from a bygone age became this Pokémon. It rambles through ruins, searching for someone who knows its face.

yamper.description: This gluttonous Pokémon only assists people with their work because it wants treats. As it runs, it crackles with electricity.

yanma.description: Its frail wings are so thin that one can see clear through them. However, during flight these wings exhibit the power to churn air with force enough to launch a house skyward.

yanmega.description: Extremely violent. When hunting, it wastes none of its energy, aiming only for prey's most vulnerable spots. Any who manage to tame this Pokémon must be of incredible bravery.

yungoos.description: Although it will eat anything, it prefers fresh living things, so it marches down streets in search of prey.

yveltal.description: When its life comes to an end, it absorbs the life energy of every living thing and turns into a cocoon once more.

zacian.description: This Pokémon has slumbered for many years. Some say it’s Zamazenta’s elder sister—others say the two Pokémon are rivals.

zamazenta.description: This Pokémon slept for aeons while in the form of a statue. It was asleep for so long, people forgot that it ever existed.

zangoose.description: Zangoose usually stays on all fours, but when angered, it gets up on its hind legs and extends its claws. This Pokémon shares a bitter rivalry with Seviper that dates back over generations.

zapdos.description: Zapdos is a legendary bird Pokémon. It’s said that when Zapdos rubs its feathers together, lightning will fall immediately after.

zarude.description: Once the vines on Zarude’s body tear off, they become nutrients in the soil. This helps the plants of the forest grow.

zebstrika.description: They have lightning-like movements. When Zebstrika run at full speed, the sound of thunder reverberates.

zekrom.description: Mythology tells us that if people lose the righteousness in their hearts, their kingdoms will be razed by Zekrom’s lightning.

zeraora.description: Electricity sparks from the pads on its limbs. Wherever Zeraora runs, lightning flashes and thunder echoes.

zigzagoon.description: Zigzagoon that adapted to regions outside Galar acquired this appearance. If you’ve lost something, this Pokémon can likely find it.

zoroark.description: With its disheveled white fur, it looks like an embodiment of death. Heedless of its own safety, Zoroark attacks its nemeses with a bitter energy so intense, it lacerates Zoroark's own body.

zorua.description: A once-departed soul, returned to life in Hisui. Derives power from resentment, which rises as energy atop its head and takes on the forms of foes. In this way, Zorua vents lingering malice.

zubat.description: Makes its home in gloomy caves. Atrophied eyes have left this Pokémon blind, so it scans its surroundings via sound waves that it emits from its mouth as it flies.

zweilous.description: Their two heads will fight each other over a single piece of food. Zweilous are covered in scars even without battling others.

zygarde-50.description: Some say it can change to an even more powerful form when battling those who threaten the ecosystem.
